#2. Elite-level incompetence is Manchester United’s problem – not Michael Carrick | Barney Ronay

Getting rid of head coach is not going to solve the problems that led to his appointment. Perhaps it’s worth, for once, doing something different

At the final whistle at Elland Road the TV cameras cut to a lingering shot of Manchester United chief executive, Omar Berrada, looking down pensively from the stands, deciding, it is to be hoped, on a little clemency, a re-sheathing of the managerial shotgun.

Here we have the man who hired the man. The man who fires the man. The man who also hired or rehired the previous two men he had to fire. Berrada was poached from Manchester City on the basis of his ability to grow commercial revenue (yes, OK, stop laughing), and appears, like everyone else with any actual reach around here, to exist in a strangely consequence-free bubble.

How do you solve what is, on revenue versus results, the worst-run club in world football? By changing the name of the latest patsy on the touchline, of course. For now a hard-fought point is perhaps enough to stave off that pre-programmed emergency response.

Stand down the cowboy cops. Call off the blue and white saloons. Although with a run of Bournemouth, Chelsea, Aston Villa and Liverpool next up in the league it will no doubt soon be time to go out there and arrest Lee Harvey Oswald again. What’s that you say? OK, well, dig him up again. Re-arrest him. Whatever it takes. Someone has to stop these lone gunmen, these managerial magic bullet merchants from derailing the Manchester United supremacy.

This was a dual-track football match between Leeds and Manchester United, on the face of it a good, even game between two teams of well-matched players. A 1-1 draw was fair in the end, although Leeds played well and probably should have won. But of course they won’t be the story.

Instead this game had already been billed as that familiar thing, a referendum on the future of Michael Carrick. A stay of execution for a week or two. Or another livestreamed firing squad for the Super Sunday cameras.

There has been a predictable sense of low comedy about Carrick’s own transformation in the United dugout this season. It was always going to be the case that his widely praised qualities in victory, blazer, T-shirt, jawline, inscrutable sense of calm, would become his fatal flaws in defeat.

Where’s the passion, the whirling arms, the range of tailored collars? At Elland Road Carrick simply looked drained in the second half as United were pegged back and overrun at times, the beard a little more ragged, the hair unkempt but still sweeping, the look of a brave, doomed tugboat captain resigned now to the approaching tsunami wave on the horizon.

A point leaves United 13th in the league and still struggling to reverse a dreadful start to the season. But it was a good game for two people. First for Carrick, who remains a million miles away from creating the problems afflicting this club, even if you accept that his presence as head coach is one of them.

Michael Carrick did not hire Michael Carrick. Getting rid of Michael Carrick is, by definition, not going to solve the problems that led to his appointment. But it might just help to prolong them. Whatever his ultimate ceiling, it is surely worth keeping him just to try, for once, to do something different.

This was also a good game for Lisandro Martínez, who went off injured at half-time with United 1-0 up, and who was also vindicated in his allegedly controversial (translation: entirely correct) comments on the club hierarchy in midweek.

United’s energetic first-half performance clarified one half of this. The players are committed in support of the manager, at least to the best of their ability. The second half made the other half of the argument, that this remains a mismatched, lopsided, cut-and-paste squad, always likely to be pulled apart by opponents as urgent as this Leeds team, which fully deserves its current seventh place in the table.

The problems are so obvious it is barely worth repeating them. But here goes. The third-richest club in the world played a second half with three of its back four out of position. Harry Maguire, signed under Ole Gunnar Solskjær, remains the best straight defender. But Maguire is also essentially a man-shaped solid wood armoire in a pair of shorts at this stage in his career, always the slowest person on any pitch, which means you will not be able to cover space, play a high line or counterattack without leaving yourself exposed to the counter-counter.

So good luck, guys. And remember Omar, who gave you this whisky bottle and loaded pistol of a squad, will be watching.

This was made painfully clear after half-time as Martínez went off and Noussair Mazraoui came on. Leeds scored an equaliser that felt structurally inevitable. They found space down their right side repeatedly. At times they seemed to be constantly peppering the seats behind the United goal, like a group of kids hammering a ball against a garage door. By the end Leeds had more possession, more shots on target and just looked a happier, better structured entity than the travelling heritage exhibit at the other end.

Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football

The key point here is to accept that all of this is entirely logical. This is not a mystery, a haunted house, a place of bad voodoo. Why do we talk about Manchester United so much? For obvious reasons. It’s a massive part of the English football landscape. Mainly, though, because this is a story of mind-bending waste, real-time elite-level incompetence played out on a weekly basis.

Yes, you could sack Michael Carrick. It won’t change much. Let’s destroy Eddie Howe for a bit instead. But the available evidence suggests every single person making executive decisions here is outmatched and outmanoeuvred.

There is a reason Manchester United feels like one of those high street legacy chain shops just before it collapses, piles of Quality Street by the door, a rat in the lingerie department, destined to become a pop-up vape shop run by Albanian money launderers. There’s a reason it feels so badly run. This is because: it is.

We know the Glazer ownership has zero interest in minding the details, that this has been a wonderful acquisition whatever the performance on the pitch, an asset supremely sweated. We know also that Sir Jim Ratcliffe is pub-level incoherent on the details he promised to fix. Remember when he was going to sit down and decide what the “style of football” would be? How’s that working out?

Instead Carrick is left shuffling a first XI acquired by endlessly revolving administrations. Here United had four defenders signed under Erik ten Hag, two Ruben Amorim recruits, two from the mist-shrouded age of Solskjær. No players were recruited under Ralf Rangnick, of course. But then Rangnick wanted to sign Erling Haaland, Luis Díaz, and Julian Álvarez, which all sounds far too sensible.

An organisation can be built with many hands. But not when so many of those hands appear to be so far from best in class it’s hard to work out which class they’re supposed to be attending. John Murtough, the former Manchester United football director, is currently director of global development at Atalanta, who have a 24,000-seat stadium and almost zero global presence. Meanwhile Berrada, the axeman, seems entirely invulnerable from the axe himself, despite the fact his job seems to orbit around resolving the consequences of his own mistakes.

United probably will sack their current manager before the year is out. This is the way this machine has to operate, always looking to buy itself, and those in the executive seats, a little more time on the payroll, an entity that has been hollowed out and allowed to rust, run on buzzwords and brown paper and string. Meanwhile, over to you Michael. We’ll see you next week, and maybe even the week after that, for more of exactly the same.

#3. Mbeumo offers Carrick solace as Man Utd winless run goes on

Manchester United's winless run extends to six games after draw with Leeds

In a season that is forcing Manchester United fans to dig deep for reasons to be positive, Bryan Mbeumo scored again at Elland Road.

That is four goals in seven Premier League games for the Cameroon forward.

Apart from Bruno Fernandes, who scored a hat-trick against Ipswich in August, no-one else in Michael Carrick's squad has scored more than one.

But it's meagre fare. It is true to say Manchester United did reasonably well in their 1-1 draw at Leeds United, just as they did at Atletico Madrid on Tuesday after conceding inside the first minute.

Carrick told BBC Radio 5 Live afterwards he "had the headphones on" this week so he hasn't heard the external noise created by Lisandro Martinez's rant.

However, he knows his side have to win matches at some point.

That is six without a victory now, the worst run since 2018-19, when form nosedived after Ole Gunnar Solskjaer was confirmed as permanent manager.

"Because they haven't lost at Leeds, we're thinking United have done all right," said former Liverpool and England defender Jamie Carragher on Sky Sports.

"But in some ways that is a negative. We are dropping the standards. We shouldn't really be talking about Manchester United like that."

Man Utd showed 'unity' in draw with Leeds - Carrick

After the corresponding fixture last season, Ruben Amorim gave the explosive press conference that triggered his dismissal within 24 hours.

This time, it was Lisandro Martinez who lit the touchpaper before the game, criticising sporting director Jason Wilcox and the United hierarchy for failing, in his view, to recruit effectively during the summer.

Wilcox was in the stands at Elland Road, while Martinez started the game following his apology for the timing and forum of his attack rather than the words themselves.

To highlight the general view that United failed Carrick by not bringing in competition for Luke Shaw at left-back, Diogo Dalot became the fifth different player to start in that position this season.

It remains to be seen if Shaw will be fit enough for Wednesday's Champions League trip to Serie A outfit Como, but the repeated changes cannot be helping Carrick.

Martinez went off at half-time with a thigh injury, and such is the delicate nature of Matthijs de Ligt's fitness after almost 11 months out with a back complaint, Carrick preferred to bring on full-back Noussair Mazraoui rather than the Netherlands international.

Carrick's side ended the game 13th in the Premier League table, with the possibility they might drop further before the match round is complete.

Unlike Amorim, Carrick found it easy to come up with a positive spin on the present situation.

"It felt like a bit of a fresh start today, to be honest, with where we're at - accepting it and doing something about it," Carrick said.

"I'm not accepting it as everything's great by any stretch. I'm realistic with that.

"But sometimes you do struggle. Sometimes there's a bit where you have to find a way through.

"There has been a cycle at times here over a period of time when it can go in different directions. We've got to be stable enough to keep doing the right things. We're more than capable of winning football matches.

"I understand the situation doesn't look too good if you look at it from a certain way, but I've got no doubts that we can go on a good run."

Manchester United sporting director Jason Wilcox (bottom centre), sat next to chief executive Omar Berrada (bottom right) at Elland Road

Calvert-Lewin scores as Leeds deny Man Utd

Everything a struggle for Fernandes - Leeds v Man Utd ratings

Free-scoring Brighton & Man United settle for a point

Manchester United striker Bryan Mbeumo (second left in huddle) celebrates scoring the opening goal against Leeds at Elland Road

Mbeumo's performance wasn't flawless by any means.

He should have done much better when he missed the target with a free header before he scored, and the former Brentford man then failed to prevent Dominic Calvert-Lewin powering in an equaliser just after half-time.

But in a campaign when so many of Carrick's attacking players are struggling â skipper Fernandes has been a shadow of the player who broke the Premier League assists record last season even though the United boss said the Portuguese was 'absolutely fine' â Mbeumo's performances have been vital.

Their importance has been heightened by the continued absence of striker Benjamin Sesko with a shin injury.

Mbeumo spent the first few games on the right of United's attack when Amad Diallo was ruled out by injury. When Amad returned, Mbeumo moved into the number nine role.

At Elland Road he was shifted again, to the left as Fernandes played more through the middle.

Bryan Mbeumo's touchmap in his past three Premier League games

"When you are the kind of player who can be very good in a lot of positions, managers will always say: 'Can you do this? Can you do that?'" former Red Devils striker Dion Dublin told BBC Sport.

"When you're in this Manchester United team at the moment, you just have to go where is best for the team."

Carrick was even more effusive in his praise.

"Bryan gives so much to the team," he said. "He sacrifices so much.

"He's willing to do pretty much anything that needs to be done to benefit the team - whether that's defending in certain areas, whether that's attacking. He'll give everything he's got.

"He's getting in really good positions to be really dangerous for us, and it's great to have him."

'Man Utd just can't seem to hold on to a lead.'

#4. De Zerbi reveals ban in latest bid to lift Spurs spirit: 'You try to find all solutions'

Please refresh the page or navigate to another page on the site to be automatically logged inPlease refresh your browser to be logged in

Fit-again Dejan Kulusevski was part of the Tottenham squad in Spain along with James Maddison

Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today.

Roberto De Zerbi has revealed a ban he put in place phones during Tottenham’s warm weather training camp in Marbella in his latest attempt to improve the camp’s spirit.

Spurs committed more than £380million on new signings this summer with 10 players joining, but they will start Monday’s home fixture with Coventry at the bottom of the Premier League.

The manager has revealed he banned phones from mealtime during Tottenham’s trip to Marbella.

“We worked on the pitch, we stayed together – we removed phones from breakfast, lunch and dinner to stay together because now it is like (phone) all the time,” De Zerbi told a press conference.

“We had two or three important meetings speaking about football, our situation and how everyone has to take responsibility. And nothing more. There were some dinners just for the players, some dinners just for the staff.

“As a coach you understand you have to improve, you have to change the situation and you try to find all solutions.

“I already did this type of training camp two times with Marseille and it was a good solution. I spoke with the club, with Vinai (Venkatesham), with Johan (Lange), with the owner and together we took the decision, but it’s nothing special.

“It’s just to spend more time together because in pre-season we couldn’t. We had many new players and players who came back from the World Cup. Three or four days together without family, putting the club at the top of their priorities, is normal and is good.”

Asked if players were able to go out independently in Marbella, De Zerbi said: “Yes, with freedom. With no military rules. I love freedom.”

Fit-again Dejan Kulusevski was part of the Tottenham squad in Spain along with James Maddison, who should face old club Coventry but is yet to start for Spurs since he damaged anterior cruciate ligaments in 2025 and Xavi Simons remains absent with the same injury.

“I am very close with Xavi Simons for example in this moment. I follow him step by step in his journey as an injured player. Like Maddison, because the management of Maddison is totally different. He is another special player and now is available to play,” De Zerbi said.

“Kulusevski was a very important player, even last season when he was injured. It is a part of this job for the players, but at the same time can be a crucial moment to become better, to become stronger.

“You need to play many games to reach the best physical condition but there are players able to be important, even if they play 10, 15 or 20 minutes and James is one player like this.

“Right now he is ready to start the game, but I don’t know if we will start with him. I’m waiting for that moment.”

#9. Man United's defence is NOT at a top-half Premier League level - Jason Wilcox and Co kicked the can down the road when it came to bolstering the backline this summer and are paying for it now, writes NATHAN SALT

Published: 23:00 BST, 18 October 2026 | Updated: 23:00 BST, 18 October 2026

Manchester United have played Hull City, Ipswich Town, Everton, Manchester City, Fulham, Tottenham Hotspur and Leeds United and failed miserably to shut out any of them.

They conceded twice against Hull, shipped two in a win over Ipswich, their only league win at this point in late October, and another two followed at Everton in a dramatic 2-2 draw.

Dominic Calvert-Lewin's goal at Leeds United ensured a third successive 1-1 draw in the Premier League and the second time in three games United have thrown victory away.

By the end, all Lisandro Martinez could do was watch on from the bench with an expression that looked totally unimpressed. Up in the stands there was a shake of the head from CEO Omar Berrada with a frustrated Jason Wilcox alongside him at the final whistle.

Defensively the foundations of this team aren't right. The higher-ups knew that in the summer and kicked the can down the road.

At this rate, with United 16th in the form table across the past four league games, that defensive rebuild won't come as a Champions League club and for that heads would have to roll.

Manchester United remain one of only two Premier League teams without a clean sheet

Director of football Jason Wilcox (third from left) has elected to fix the defence next summer

Of the 20 teams in the Premier League this season, only TWO have failed to keep a single clean sheet. Manchester United are one of them. Newly promoted Ipswich are the other.

That should be surprising. Martinez and his team-mates did not look surprised, though.

After all, they started at Elland Road with a right back at left back, a centre-back at right back, and finished with a right back at centre-back with a right winger at right wing-back and a right back at left wing-back. Square pegs, round holes.

They oscillated between a back five and a back four and yet by the end were grateful to have secured a point.

There's no Luke Shaw, out injured in a totally believable scenario before the season began. There's no Patrick Dorgu who, in truth, isn't a left back. Noussair Mazraoui, back involved after a period out injured, looked predictably uncomfortable and unsure as a centre-back. It was his mismatch from a corner that allowed Leeds to score.

Martinez, after a strong first 45 minutes that represented the best defensive half of United's season so far, was forced off with a knock at the interval. United looked significantly worse without him.

United have an enormously long list when it comes to what they must fix right now.

They must find a way to bring Bruno Fernandes, operating as a false nine here, into form as he once again struggled. They must be clinical when the chances arrive. Carrick must make better decisions in-game, too, with substitutions here failing to make the side better.

United are proving a soft touch at the back and cannot progress by conceding every match

Lisandro Martinez (middle) looked unimpressed as United conceded after his substitution

But crucially, they must become harder to score against. Right now, they aren't – and opponents are smelling blood in the water.

'When you come to places like this, you can't be beaten on set plays and we conceded a set play which got them back in the game,' Harry Maguire, who individually did play well and won Player of the Match at Elland Road, said.

'Throughout we felt comfortable in our [back three] shape. They didn't create too many chances. To concede a set-piece after half-time is disappointing. We had to dig in.'

There are technical complaints and structural ones, too, no doubt. There have been fine margins – the Man City goal at Old Trafford shouldn't have stood, for one.

But in their heart of hearts, these United defenders, however short they have been left by those upstairs (and they have by the way), have got to want to defend and want to become hard to play against.

They simply aren't brave enough. Maguire agrees.

'We're in a circumstance where we are not as brave as we should be, and we have to get that back because to win games for Man Utd we have to have that bravery and composure,' he said.

Laid bare that one of this side's most experienced players, a former captain, explicitly stated that this back-line isn't brave enough. That's as damning as anything Martinez said in the mixed zone after losing to Atletico Madrid.

Harry Maguire, who actually played well, accused United of not being brave enough defending

Let's not forget that this is a backline that has Maguire and Martinez both out of contract in 2027. The club hold the option to extend both and may well do so. But surely both must earn it? Dalot, too, is under the microscope ahead of this supposed defensive rebuild next summer. Shaw is out of contract next June and what of the long-term prospects of players like Mazraoui? The bar by which these players are being judged is getting lower by the week.

Drawing at Leeds means that United have won just one of their seven Premier League matches this season (D4, L2), their fewest number of wins at this stage of a top-flight campaign since 1986-87.

Wilcox and Co kicked the can down the road when it came to bolstering the backline and are paying for it now.

'This is not a club at Champions League level,' Martinez fumed in Madrid.

Right now they aren't at a top-half Premier League level.

Fail to fix their defence on the fly and this could get a whole lot worse before it gets better for United.

#11. Keira Walsh targeting the last trophy missing in her collection

The Chelsea midfielder is eyeing up the game's biggest prize next year

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

With five league titles, two Champions Leagues and a host of domestic cup winners' medals in her collection, Chelsea midfielder Keira Walsh has won just about everything there is to win in women's football.

This success also extends to the international scene, where the 29-year-old was part of England's two European Championship successes in 2022 and 2025.

However, there is one notable trophy missing from her CV - the World Cup.

Walsh played both legs of England's 8-1 aggregate win over Greece, which secured their place in the two-legged World Cup play-off against Ukraine in November, the winner of which will seal their place in Brazil for next summer's tournament.

This play-off run has come after Spain pipped the Lionesses to top spot in their qualifying group on goal difference, underlining just had challenging even making the finals is.

"The same way we'd approach any game," Walsh told FourFourTwo about the team's play-off test.

"It’s difficult to qualify now in the initial stages because there’s two or three top teams in each group, so it's really, really difficult."

The best features, fun and footballing quizzes, straight to your inbox every week.

This is a point emphasised by the fact that England were paired with world champions Spain, who defeated them 1-0 in the World Cup final back in 2023, as Walsh came agonisingly close to completing her set of major honours.

But rather than dwell on the past, the former Barcelona midfielder is fixated on her side's next match.

"For us in the next stage, it's the same as any game," she continues.

"We want to win, we want to go to the World Cup and we know what we need to do to get there. We know what we need to improve as a group and as individuals. So I'm excited to meet back up and hit the ground running."

And what about adding that elusive final trophy to her collection?

"Yeah, literally! And that definitely gives me motivation. I'm getting on a little bit as well so I'm aware that it could be my last World Cup. So it's a big year."

For more than a decade, Joe Mewis has worked in football journalism as a reporter and editor. Mewis has had stints at Mirror Football and LeedsLive among others and worked at FourFourTwo throughout Euro 2024, reporting on the tournament. In addition to his journalist work, Mewis is also the author of four football history books that include times on Leeds United and the England national team. Now working as a digital marketing coordinator at Harrogate Town, too, Mewis counts some of his best career moments as being in the iconic Spygate press conference under Marcelo Bielsa and seeing his beloved Leeds lift the Championship trophy during lockdown.

#12. Madueke breaks Nottingham Forest’s resistance as dogged Arsenal edge to victory

The theme before kick-off was blanks. Or, more precisely, whether either team could stop firing them at the City Ground. It was a detail to make Oliver Glasner extremely uncomfortable that his Nottingham Forest team had still to score at their own stadium this season. Arsenal, meanwhile, had drawn 0-0 on their previous two visits to this part of the east Midlands. They had only one win in five here.

Forest’s frustrations under their new manager go on. It was another spirited performance from them, bits to like, especially a full-throttle performance from Liam Delap in the No 9 position. But, for the fifth time under Glasner, there was not a goal to celebrate in front of the home support.

It was a game that came to feel increasingly set up for the famous terrace chant. One-nil to the Ars-en-nal. Or, as the travelling hordes would have it, one-nil to the champions. Arsenal did not play well. They created little, finishing with just one shot on target. How Noni Madueke made it count.

On as a half-time substitute, the winger took a pass from Declan Rice in the 80th minute and had only one thing on his mind. To cut inside from the left and unload. The connection was pure and that was when he caught a break, which he has worked to earn after a difficult start to the season. The ball deflected off Jair Cunha and flew past the Forest goalkeeper, Matz Sels.

Forest refused to accept the inevitable. Chris Wood, on as a substitute, delayed too long and saw Rice block. Murillo, of all players, danced inside from the left and curled off target. Delap was denied at the death by a thunderous Ezri Konsa block tackle. But it did feel inevitable. Forest, who missed the injured Morgan Gibbs-White, might have played all night and not scored. Arsenal had not forgotten their previous away fixture – the 3-0 defeat at Brighton. It remains the only blot on their season.

Arsenal had kicked off six points behind Manchester City, who have been perfect on the field in the league this season. Will it matter when the sanctions for their rule breaches are meted out? All Arsenal can do is play the situation as it stands and this was an occasion when the result was everything.

Mikel Arteta’s team dominated the ball. As they were always likely to do. They were determined to be patient. And yet they were flat and predictable until the closing stages. The lack of incisive movement was glaring. That said, Forest were compact out of possession in a 5-4-1 formation and hard to break down. They were resolved not to give up any easy yards.

Arsenal played their patterns. They tried to suck the life out of the home crowd, working on the principle that it is difficult for fans to get animated if their team do not have the ball. The first half drifted by in a lazy Sunday afternoon haze, no shots on target for either side.

Delap carried the physical fight; the Forest centre-forward was a willing and direct runner and he won a free-kick off Rice just outside the Arsenal box on 44 minutes. Neco Williams thumped it at Bruno Guimarães, who went down and stayed down. The Forest support were unhappy at what they perceived as Arsenal’s use of the dark arts. “Are you City in disguise?” they chanted.

Could a set piece provide the breakthrough? It felt the likeliest route. Murillo headed wide from a Forest corner in the 20th minute and was bloodied into the bargain; there was a whistle for a foul in the mass of bodies inside the six-yard box. At the other end, Kai Havertz headed over from a Rice free-kick on 37 minutes. He had a good look at the ball and was well-placed. It was a decent chance.

Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football

Arsenal have been a little barren in the first half this season. This was the seventh time in 10 matches since the Community Shield that they had failed to score in one. It has not been a problem. They needed to raise their levels for the second half.

Arteta’s first change was Madueke for Eberechi Eze on the left wing; an admission that the latter had failed to exert an influence. There was also a triple substitution on 66 minutes, the manager sending on Jurriën Timber, Mikel Merino and Viktor Gyökeres for Ben White, Guimarães and Havertz. He needed to shake things up because nothing was happening for his team. It was Forest who pushed after the restart, with Delap continuing to put himself about. He asked questions of Gabriel Magalhães, albeit the Arsenal defender tended to have the answers.

The minutes ticked down, the contest narrowing to a fine point and we waited to see whether there could be a moment, one big chance. Martin Ødegaard almost provided it in the 72nd minute when he released Timber with a lovely pass up the inside right. When he pulled back, Rice lifted wastefully high.

Glasner’s decision to introduce Ibrahim Sangaré for Dan Ndoye shortly afterwards was telling. Sangaré’s mission was to bolster the Forest midfield and yet he was slow to react to a half-cleared ball. When Rice played the pass, Madueke took over.

“We showed a champion spirit,” Madueke said. “Maybe last season, this game might not have gone for us. We have the extra belief and mentality.”

#13. Madueke's 'anger and conviction' shows he's more than a 'finisher'

Madueke's strike enough as Arsenal pick up narrow win over Forest

Noni Madueke may not have the starting role he wants at Arsenal, but his winning goal against Nottingham Forest showed why he is one of Mikel Arteta's valued "finishers".

The England international scored in the second half to earn Arsenal a 1-0 result and three valuable points towards their defence of the Premier League title.

Madueke has started just one top-flight game this season, the 2-1 win over Leeds that came eight days prior to their victory over Oliver Glasner's Forest on Sunday.

Arsenal's summer was dominated by talk of their search for an elite forward, with the left wing one of the positions identified.

But after unsuccessful pursuits of superstar players such as Vinicius Jr and Julian Alvarez, the only new addition in that position was Christos Tzolis, the winger brought in to replace the outgoing Leandro Trossard.

Tzolis has started the season well and has been the first-choice winger for Arteta, meaning that Madueke and Eberechi Eze have had to be content with the majority of their minutes coming from the bench or in the Carabao Cup.

However, Tzolis is now out with a hamstring injury picked up while playing for Greece, and that has presented a chance for Madueke to show Arteta why he should be considering the former Chelsea man as much more than a finisher - the term Arteta uses for his substitutes.

Madueke did well when starting against Leeds, praised by Arteta for being the best player at the club during the international break. The Arsenal boss said the winger "grabbed it [his start] with both hands".

The England international also started on the right wing, his more natural position, against Lille in a Champions League win on Tuesday, assisting the opening goal.

Against Forest on Sunday, Madueke was introduced at half-time by Arteta and said he took the manager's instructions with him on to the pitch.

"Hang in there, stick to the gameplan, go out there and try to attack the opposition, be dangerous, be yourself and be good defensively as well," Madueke said.

He scored with a deflected shot in the 80th minute when he took on defender Daniel Munoz and cut in on his weaker right foot.

"I'd beaten him on the outside a couple of times so I thought I'll come inside and just let rip," Madueke said.

Noni Madueke has scored two goals this season in all competitions for Arsenal.

It's fair to say that the Arsenal fans have not always taken to Madueke since his move from London rivals Chelsea.

There was a 'No to Madueke' petition started when he joined the club and his performances have been criticised for being inconsistent.

But since his Â£48.5m arrival, Madueke has helped the club lift their first Premier League title in 22 years and played a big part as Arsenal reached the Champions League final.

Madueke scored eight goals and provided four assists in 43 appearances in all competitions last season, but questions over his end product remain.

He is one of Arsenal's most direct players, and England manager Thomas Tuchel and his staff also rate the winger as one of the best players in one-versus-one situations.

"Noni, look at me, a smile on my face because he is a special character," Arteta said when he was asked about Madueke's character.

"It's someone that's very much loved in and around the dressing room. The way he connects, talks with people. He is just a special guy.

"I think I saw an interview where they were asking a few of our players 'who would you call if you had a problem?' And some of them said Noni, which I was surprised.

"But I think it is a massive credit and describes the type of person he is."

The 24-year-old has now put in three good performances in a row.

"He is in a good moment," Arteta said. "After the break, he is showing something else, another level of anger, another level of conviction as well as in his actions and he is becoming decisive in matches, which is what we expect from a player like him.

"He is a player that doesn't really mind left or right, but he has played many more minutes on the right side. The team needs him there at the moment and he is doing well."

Madueke scores as Arsenal win tight game at Forest

Arteta's verdict on Arsenal's win at Nottingham Forest

Arteta has made a big point of referring to his substitutes as "finishers" as he points to the importance of the squad.

That mentality is seeming to have the desired effect. Since the start of last season, Arsenal substitutes have contributed to 26 Premier League goals, which is more than any other side in the league.

Bruno Guimaraes scored the winner against Leeds after coming off the bench last time out in the league, while substitutes Bukayo Saka, Kai Havertz and captain Martin Odegaard played a major role in the last two goals in the win over Lille.

But Arteta is not concerned the Gunners are overly reliant on players from the bench.

"There have been other games as well that we have had to score in the first half," Arteta said.

"We have played 11 competitive matches and we won 10. We are getting a variety of ways to win in many different contexts."

Arteta said he expected few chances against a well organised Forest at the City Ground but added: "I had the belief that the moment the physical level was going to drop, the spaces would be a little bit bigger, the timing more and we would be more efficient there.

"And the finishers delivered because the context of the game changed a little bit."

Please refresh the page or navigate to another page on the site to be automatically logged inPlease refresh your browser to be logged in

England star James fired a brace versus Spurs as Chelsea kept up their chase of dominant league leaders City, who almost let a three-goal lead slip versus Brighton

Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today.

Manchester City maintained a perfect start to their Women’s Super League campaign but were made to sweat after holding off a Brighton fightback.

Andree Jeglertz’s side were three goals in front after 17 minutes thanks to a double from Khadjia Shaw and a first goal for summer signing Niamh Charles. Brighton, however, fought back through goals from Olivia Garcia and Caitlin Hayes.

And Jeglertz was not overly impressed by how his team took their foot of the gas.

“I don’t think the players did it on purpose, becoming more comfortable. As a team, we just became more comfortable,” he said. “It wasn’t the same speed on our passes or supporting each other in the same way. We let them in by going down a couple of percent.

“They scored two goals which was unnecessary. I was a little bit annoyed [at half-time]. There was no yelling. They don’t do it on purpose. It becomes a little bit automatic. It was more a reminder to go back to everything we did in the beginning and do everything 100%. We bounced back.”

City remain two points ahead of Chelsea, who turned on the style in the second half to defeat Tottenham 6-2 at Stamford Bridge.

Lauren James and Ellie Carpenter both notched braces for Sonia Bompastor’s side. Spurs were level at the break thanks to Matilda Vinberg but three goals in nine blistering second-half minutes swung the game Chelsea’s way. Substitutes Maika Hamano and Sjoeke Nusken also found the net.

“I'm pleased with the performance and the result,” said Bompastor, who was taking charge of her 50th WSL game. “I was convinced coming into this game, we would need players who would come in and bring a big impact and fresh legs.

“On the back of the international break, we can talk about the tactical aspects, but it was probably the most important thing to have players who impacted the game the way they did today. So it's good when you have depth in the squad, a lot of players available, and the quality of the players who are coming in.”

London City Lionesses made it a full house for the top three, beating Everton 2-1.

First-half goals from Delphine Cascarino and England winger Freya Godfrey had seemingly put the Lionesses in control. Everton, though, set up a tense finish after substitute Holly McNamara headed in with 20 minutes left.

Manchester United climbed to fifth after a third successive win, seeing off bottom side Charlton 3-1. Three goals in the opening quarter of an hour saw Ella Toone and Andrea Medina put United two up before Leah Davidson pulled one back. Julia Zigioitti Olme completed the scoring just after the half-hour mark.

Aston Villa stunned Liverpool, coming from behind to secure a 2-1 win for their first league win of the season. Natalia Ramos scored a spectacular early opener, but Villa improved after half-time, with Chasity Grant firing in an equaliser before a Grace Fisk own goal.

Kelly Gago scored the only goal in the first half as West Ham defeated Crystal Palace 1-0.

#21. Hearts roll out red carpet ... and Celtic walk all over it

Stephen Kingsley and Jamie McCart cannot stop Celtic scoring a fifth

Jimmy Thunder was having none of Crawford Grimsley's chutzpah, none of his mouthing off before their heavyweight contest back in the late 1990s, none of his pre-bout arrogance.

Thunder took precisely 1.5 seconds to put Grimsley down - one punch, an overhand right to his opponent's temple. Lights out. Fight over. Statement sent.

As Celtic unloaded on Hearts at Celtic Park it was football's equivalent of Thunder's devastation; speed and accuracy and ruthlessness in the face of a challenger akin to a rabbit caught in the headlights.

Hearts didn't give it the big one in the preamble to this evisceration, but they set up in the manner of a team who truly believed they were a whole lot better than they actually are.

Poor concentration and lack of physicality cost them two set-piece goals inside 10 minutes. The game was effectively over, but the visitors' suffering had only just begun.

Celtic score seven in humiliation of title rivals Hearts

All the latest Celtic news, views and analysis

The pretenders came to Glasgow with a weak away record in the league - two wins in 11 between this season and the end of last, both against Hibs - and tried to go toe-to-toe.

Thinking attack is the best form of defence is all very well as long as you can back it up, as long as you can defend competently, as long as you can pass from A to B without losing your mind, as long as you don't concede acreage of space to exploit.

Time and again, Hearts rolled out the red carpet to Celtic.

A clinical Celtic made them pay for their naivety and maybe their arrogance, too. The footballing version of poor Crawford Grimsley. On their backside before they knew it.

Hearts played the highest line with slow defenders, they pushed up the park and left themselves exposed to Celtic's speedsters. That gameplan was not high-risk, it was reckless.

Martin O'Neill needed a win after his recent travails and this was a stroll in the park that he could not have imagined.

Football management can be a horribly stressful business that can put years on you. After this, O'Neill looked younger not older. The ageing process worked in reverse thanks to his team feasting on Hearts' scarcely believable weaknesses.

The stats are, frankly, hilarious. If it was a horrific day for Wouter Vrancken and his players then it was every bit as grim an experience for those who try to see sense in numbers.

Hearts had more shots than Celtic (20-18). They had more shots inside the box (16-13). They had more possession (52%-48%). They had more crosses (16-10). They won more duels (51%-49%). They had more passes in their opponents' half (244-202). They had more accurate passes (458-423).

That last one was laugh-out-loud funny, for Hearts' use of the ball was comically bad.

So often, when under a little bit of pressure, or no pressure at all, they passed into space only for Celtic to gobble up the loose ball and launch an attack which usually ended in a big chance or a goal.

The home team was slick. Benjamin Nygren, Callum Osmand, Camilo Duran and Haissem Hassan were devastating. Seven did not flatter them in the slightest.

It began with those two early goals - Liam Scales showing the desire to win a near-post header from a corner and Kieran Tierney left alone a few yards out to force in, then Dane Murray outfighting Claudio Braga to help it back to Nygren to score.

Hassan hit a post when he turned and darted away from Stephen Kingsley. People wondered what was Vrancken going to do to change this. Answer: nothing.

'Elated, delighted, relieved' - O'Neill on Celtic's thrashing of Hearts

When Celtic score seven it seems odd to talk about pieces of defending they did that were significant, but Colby Donovan's cameos warrant mention.

Around the midpoint of the first half, Hearts stirred a little. You wouldn't say that they had momentum, but they had a bit of a possession and their hair-on-fire panic of the early minutes seemed under control.

Twice in the space of three minutes, Josh McPake - one of the form players in the country - took on Donovan and twice Donovan routed him.

Those little duels might disappear from relevance after the deluge, but at the time they were important. The Hearts dangerman had been snuffed out. His morale had taken a hiding. And the stadium loved it.

Hearts fell apart at the seams from there. Sabri Guendouz gave the ball away and Duran combined with the impressive Osmand to score number three.

Jamie McCart then became detached from his trolley and Celtic scored from that error, too. Osmand, again, but with lovely work from Duran. And easy, oh so easy.

Celtic's pace in attack was terrific. Their alertness was outstanding. Their disbelief was there, too. How could a team with a seemingly good coach and a strong squad of players be performing like a pub team?

Hearts fans started heading home at that point. They missed the goal that made it 4-1. They won't have shed any tears. Had they gone back they'd only have suffered on. Best get out of dodge as quickly as possible.

Soon, it was 5-1, Mika Baur slaloming his way past the comatose figures of McPake and Malachi Fagan-Walcott to dink a shot on goal, helped on its way by Kingsley and McCart, sitting on the floor, all flailing legs, like an octopus who had fallen out of a tree.

Hearts performance 'not acceptable' but Vrancken 'won't kill players'

Hearts' heads had long since gone. They were a broken team, psychologically. The doubt and fear coursed through their veins.

The easiest things became difficult. The difficult things became impossible. They had no discipline, no direction.

Vrancken spoke later about individual errors and that was obvious, but what else? He was given an opportunity to take some responsibility for the way he set his team up to begin with, but he declined to go there.

On reflection, maybe he will. He should. Gung-ho football is fine when it works. Unless it's laced with some pragmatism when facing the best teams in their own backyard then it can blow up in your face, which it did at Celtic Park.

Then it was 6-1 (Laurent Mendy the culprit, followed by McCart) and 7-1 (Tomas Magnusson in the frame). Duran and Nygren finished with aplomb. Seven minutes remained. The expectation was that this could still become eight or nine.

We like to think this league title race can be a three-horse thing again this season. We want the drama of last time.

Hearts played Celtic four times last term. They won two, drew one and lost one. They had nous and resilience before it all slowly slipped away from them.

This team has talent but, with their away record as it is, they're not going the distance, or anything close to the distance.

Celtic will be buoyed by this. Using it as fuel is the next step.

Osmand was a big player for them. O'Neill might have hit on a powerful front three that doesn't involve Kasper Hogh from the start.

After some rough days and nights they have some of their feelgood back. Keeping it on the long road ahead is the challenge now.

#23. Gómez halfway-line wondergoal sparks Brighton’s 5-0 thrashing of sorry Crystal Palace

At last, Fabian Hürzeler has the scalp that matters most to all Brighton fans and in humiliating fashion. Diego Gómez’s breathtaking goal-of-the-season contender from the halfway line, à la David Beckham, was the highlight of another hugely impressive performance from the Premier League’s top scorers as they continued their flying start to the season.

Not since a 4-1 thrashing here in February 2024 under Roberto De Zerbi had Brighton tasted victory against their arch rivals from up the A23 – a run of four matches. But having been handed the initiative by Jaydee Canvot’s own goal, a stunned Palace found themselves 3-0 down after 10 minutes. It got even worse for Pierre Sage after Brighton extended their lead through Gómez’s wonderstrike and Yasin Ayari, with Charalampos Kostoulas adding a fourth after half-time and the substitute Jack Hinshelwood’s late strike matching their record 5-0 win over Palace from 1956 in Division Three South.

The concerning news for Sage, whose decision to field the teenager Honest Ahanor and 20-year-old Canvot in defence backfired spectacularly, is that two of his predecessors – Patrick Vieira and Roy Hodgson – were relieved of their jobs not long after losing against Brighton. Palace have conceded more goals than any other Premier League side this season and it is understood that there have been some disagreements behind the scenes since the Frenchman took over from Oliver Glasner in the summer, although it remains to be seen whether the chair, Steve Parish, will act on suggestions from the gleeful Brighton supporters during the second half that he will be sacked in the morning.

“It’s not my decision. I don’t know,” said Sage when asked if he will be given time to fix Palace’s leaky defence. “I will always give my best. I just want to apologise to the fans because it’s not normal to show this face. My feeling after the game is shame.”

It was Hürzleler who was on the receiving end of that chant in February after Palace’s smash-and-grab victory on the south coast. How things have changed. His vibrant side now find themselves in the conversation for Champions League qualification and they have a squad that also looks capable of coping with the demands of European football.

“The last game against Palace made me really grounded, having this criticism. It wasn’t easy,” said Hürzeler. “Now we sit here in a completely different mood, with a feeling of being really proud to beat Palace. I experienced some derbies and I’m part of this club, I’m part of the journey, that’s why I’m also part of the history. The players deserve it for the hard work they did in the last month because they really stuck together, they faced adversity. They were always there for each other.”

The usual hostility greeted the travelling fans after Sussex police had warned they would be deploying extra officers to deal with what remains very much a grudge match. But a torrential downpour before kick-off didn’t dampen Brighton’s desire for revenge. They tore into Palace’s inexperienced defence from the first whistle and Canvot was caught flat-footed as he headed a pinpoint free-kick from Pascal Gross past Walter Benítez.

The Palace goalkeeper could then only watch in horror when Olivier Boscagli fed Gómez on the halfway line after Adam Wharton had lost possession cheaply and the ball sailed over his head into the net after the sweetest of contacts. No wonder that Hürzeler has been urging his players to take more shots from long range this season – they were already the division’s top scorers with efforts from outside the box this season with four. Gómez’s strike from 51 metres was the Premier League goal from furthest out since Wayne Rooney scored from 58 metres for Everton against West Ham in November 2017.

Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football

Things got even better for Brighton when a flowing move down the right allowed Kostoulas to tee up Ayari to sweep home via a deflection off the unfortunate Canvot. Sage looked like he wanted the ground to swallow him up.

If he hoped things might improve after the break then he was mistaken. It took Kostoulas only four minutes to make it 4-0 after the ball deflected into his path after good work from Gross. To the delight of the Brighton fans, Jean-Philippe Mateta contrived to hit the crossbar with the goal gaping on his return from injury before Eddie Nketiah also fluffed the chance to grab a consolation.

Sage’s assistant, Paddy McCarthy, had to be held back from confronting the Brighton bench, with tempers threatening to spill over. Plenty of Palace fans had already seen enough by then as they made their escape after a nightmarish afternoon. They missed Hinshelwood scoring from close range six minutes from the end to round off the perfect afternoon for Hürzeler, who could not hide his emotion as he celebrated with his players at full time.

#24. Mikel Arteta hails Arsenal's resilience and ability to 'suffer' in gritty victory at Nottingham Forest but makes tactical admission - as Gunners boss lays down challenge to 'special' Noni Madueke after matchwinning cameo

Published: 22:30 BST, 18 October 2026 | Updated: 22:30 BST, 18 October 2026

Mikel Arteta hailed the way his Arsenal players managed to ‘suffer’ and break down Nottingham Forest’s defensive ‘Christmas tree’ set-up to earn victory.

Substitute Noni Madueke’s 80th-minute strike sealed the match as Arsenal’s only shot on target, with Arteta’s bench once again coming to the rescue.

The north London club dominated possession with little joy around the penalty area before four second-half changes, including Madueke, helped change the tide.

It’s now six wins from seven in the Premier League for the Gunners who sit in second place, three points behind Manchester City.

Arteta said: ‘We’ve played 11 competitive matches and won 10. So we're going to get a variety of ways to win in many different contexts. We knew today we wouldn't score in the first 20-30 minutes.

’We were going to face a different Forest because they're extremely well covered. They put a Christmas tree (3-4-1-2) there. There's no space to play. You have to be so neat and tidy. You have to otherwise generate a lot of chaos in the box, whether it's in open play or with set-pieces.

Mikel Arteta praised his Arsenal stars for 'suffering' to break down Nottingham Forest's Christmas tree-style defence

He hailed Noni Madueke for reaching 'another level' - but says he 'expects' such performances from the match-winning winger

’We didn't even hit the target, which is the difference. And the longer the game goes, we say, “OK, now we have to play a different game because the moment we start to ramp up our level of frustration, the game is going to be really dangerous for us because we're going to take more risks than we should”.

‘I had the belief that the moment the physical level was going to drop, the spaces would be a little bit bigger. And the finishing delivered because the game changed and the context of that game changed a little bit. And then we have to suffer because we had two or three actions that were a bit strange to witness.’

On Madueke’s display, he added: ‘There's a smile on my face because he's a special character.

‘He's just a special guy. He's in a good moment. I think after the break he's showing something else, another level of anger, another level of conviction as well in his actions and he's becoming decisive in matches, which is what we expect from a player like him.’

Goalscorer Madueke was effusive about the impact of Arsenal’s ‘absurd’ bench to get the three points.

Madueke said: ‘We had to dig deep, we know it's difficult to come here. Thank God we were able to get the win and we move on with three points.

‘If you look at the quality of our starting XI and bench it's absurd so we know that we're going to start some and finish some and for me it's the same mentality every time. I just want to create or score.

‘Amazing feeling [to score] but I feel better about the win.’

#26. The ‘absurd’ part of this Arsenal team that can help champions defend their Premier League crown

Please refresh the page or navigate to another page on the site to be automatically logged inPlease refresh your browser to be logged in

Nottingham Forest 0-1 Arsenal: Noni Madueke came off the bench to earn the Gunners a third successive win

Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today.

Modern football is a game of two parts: the first hour or so, dictated by carefully curated gameplans and training ground patterns; and the final half-hour when a flurry of substitutes come on, rigid structures fade away and a match opens at the seams. Arsenal were dire for most of this game at the City Ground, shut out by Nottingham Forest’s red wall. But yet again the power of Mikel Arteta’s “finishers” decided a match.

Noni Madueke was sent on at half-time for Eberechi Eze, who had been statuesque at his station on the left touchline, which, in fairness, is not his position. With the clock ticking towards 80 minutes, Madueke did what Eze hadn’t and drove at Forest’s defence before unleashing a shot, which took a fortunate deflection off Jair Cunha on its way past the helpless Matz Sels. It went down as Arsenal’s only shot on target, and in truth it might have been curling wide.

This was the third game in a row in which Arteta rang the changes in the second half as his team struggled to click, after Leeds last weekend and Lille in midweek. Once again he made a triple substitution on 65 minutes, sending on Jurrien Timber, Mikel Merino and Viktor Gyokeres, and once again a stubborn defence was worn down in the final stages. No Premier League side has generated more goals and assists from the bench since the start of last season.

Forest were excellent in their determination to blunt Arsenal’s attack. Like Eze, Kai Havertz and Bukayo Saka had little joy, and Oliver Glasner took positives from a performance of cohesion and spirit. Liam Delap was a brilliant nuisance in attack and could have equalised in the final minutes but for Ezri Konsa’s last-ditch block. Murillo nearly scored the goal of the season, dribbling in from the left touchline before curling just over the bar with one of the last kicks. But Forest remain third from bottom after a third successive defeat, and their wait for a first home goal of the season goes on.

Arsenal, meanwhile, stay second, three points behind Manchester City and two ahead of Brighton. Second might be enough for first when City are eventually sanctioned. And even if Arsenal endure more struggles like they did for the majority of this game, strength in depth may prove the difference between the champions and the rest.

“If you look at the quality of our starting XI and bench, it’s absurd,” said Madueke, after a game in which fellow substitutes Max Dowman, Martin Zubimendi and Myles Lewis-Skelly weren’t needed. “We know that we’re going to start some [games] and finish some, and for me it’s the same mentality every time: I just want to create or score.

“All 20-something players are elite and of the highest level. It’s great to have that type of competition, you know on the bench you’re ready to have an impact.”

Arteta added: “Some of them played three days ago and some of them will start the next game, and they know that everyone has to be at it. If you are needed after 60 minutes, 45 minutes and sometimes two minutes, we have a squad now that can deliver in moments and we have to use that.”

It had been a desperate game. For those who rail against the hegemony of positional football, who say it’s shackling ingenuity and entertainment, this first half was exhibit A. Arsenal had 74% possession and no shots on target. Gabriel would pass the ball out to Eze on the touchline who would recycle it back into the middle, rinse and repeat.

“Arsenal have been the better team,” said Roy Keane at half-time, and he was right, in the sense that they are literally the better team. But better at what, exactly? Better at keeping the ball away from opposition’s prying toes, perhaps, better at that square pass Declan Rice makes to a centre-back after deciding against a forward ball.

With 331 passes at a completion rate of 91%, Arsenal were certainly better at fluffing their own statistics, although Forest didn’t help themselves: during one of many lulls, Ivorian centre-back Ousmane Diomande passed the ball straight off the pitch, chest high, nowhere near anybody, with the conviction of a man executing a plan only he knew existed.

But when it came to the nuts and bolts of the game, to tackling, to running, to winning duels, it was hard to tell the two sides apart. After 45 stultifying minutes in which neither goalkeeper made a save, it was actually Forest who had taken five of the game’s eight shots.

Rice was particularly impotent playing as the six at the base of midfield. It is a role which showcases very little of his greatest trait, his athleticism, but with Lewis-Skelly on the bench, Guimaraes was given licence to rove forwards with Martin Odegaard. The pair occasionally injected brief moments of speed into Arsenal’s game but no one else found their wavelength. It wasn’t a great surprise to see Eze replaced by Madueke at half-time, but Arsenal met the same problems.

Then came Arteta’s triple change: Merino for Guimaraes, Timber for Ben White, Gyokeres for Havertz. Forest dropped deeper and on 71 minutes, Arsenal produced their best move of the match when Saka played a short pass inside to Odegaard, who slipped in Timber running around the back of the Forest defence. Timber teed up Rice, who slashed a shot over the bar from 12 yards.

But Madueke rode to the rescue, dribbling inside to score after Merino had first forced back Forest’s centre-backs with a dangerous run.

“He’s a special character,” Arteta added of Madueke. “He’s someone who everyone loves in and around the dressing room with the way he connects and talks to people. I think I saw an interview where they were asking our players, ‘Who would you call if you have a problem?’ and some of them said, ‘Noni’, which I was surprised at. But I think it’s a massive credit and explains the kind of character that he is.

“We knew today we wouldn’t score in the first 20, 30 minutes. We were going to face a different Forest because they are extremely well coached, they put like a Christmas tree [formation], there is no space to play. You have to be so neat and tidy. You have to generate a lot of chaos in the box, whether that is an open play or with set-pieces.

“At the end I had the belief that the physical level [of Forest] was going to drop, the spaces will be a little bit bigger, more time to be more efficient. And the finishers delivered.”

The forward returned to Forest in 2014 after being rejected as a teenager

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Throughout the second half of the 2010s, Britt Assombalonga made his name as one of the Championship's most prolific strikers.

After making his senior debut at Watford, he would work his way through the divisions, scoring goals on loan at Wealdstone, Braintree Town and Southend United before making a permanent move to Peterborough, where a 33-goal season earned him a move to Nottingham Forest.

When he made this 2014 switch, the Congolese forward was returning to the club that had rejected him as a teenager.

Assombalonga had a trial at the City Ground when he was just 14, but was not able to earn himself a permanent deal. The experience, however, left a lasting impression on the youngster, meaning his change to finally pull on the famous Garibaldi red shirt meant even more to him.

From the colour and noise of the City Ground to the bitter rivalry with Derby County, Assombalonga's spell back at Forest was a career-defining stint for him.

"I’d actually been on trial at Forest when I was 14 and, while it didn’t work out, the club left a massive impression on me," he admits to FourFourTwo.

While this trial did not work out for him, the 10-time DR Congo international refused to bear a grudge.

The best features, fun and footballing quizzes, straight to your inbox every week.

"I’d always dreamt of going back and proving them wrong," he continues. "Not that I ever held it against them – these things happen – but I felt I had unfinished business there."

When Assombalonga joined Forest for a £5million fee from Peterborough in 2014, he immediately fell for the team, the fans and their famous stadium.

"The City Ground is amazing, honestly," he adds. "When the crowd is behind the team and the place is rocking, there are few atmospheres like it."

Never is this atmosphere so raw as when Forest play their most bitter rivals.

"Especially when we played Derby – I can always remember how fierce the atmosphere was in those games due to the history between the clubs and the fact they’re so close.

"I really felt like I was playing for a massive club that had historical importance to English football. I loved my time at Forest and I’m really proud to have scored the goals I did there."

For more than a decade, Joe Mewis has worked in football journalism as a reporter and editor. Mewis has had stints at Mirror Football and LeedsLive among others and worked at FourFourTwo throughout Euro 2024, reporting on the tournament. In addition to his journalist work, Mewis is also the author of four football history books that include times on Leeds United and the England national team. Now working as a digital marketing coordinator at Harrogate Town, too, Mewis counts some of his best career moments as being in the iconic Spygate press conference under Marcelo Bielsa and seeing his beloved Leeds lift the Championship trophy during lockdown.

#31. Sage feels 'shame' at Palace thrashing with future in doubt

Pierre Sage post match interview - Brighton v Crystal Palace

Crystal Palace manager Pierre Sage said he felt "shame" at the Eagles' performance during their 5-0 thrashing by Brighton and did not know whether he would be given time to save his job.

Sage's side conceded three times in the opening 10 minutes as they suffered their worst loss to their rivals since January 1956.

"It's my fault because I am the coach, I gave the motivation. I prepare the situations. We played so bad it's my fault," said Frenchman Sage, who was only appointed Palace manager in the summer.

"It's difficult to summarise because there are a lot of negative points.

"We started really bad. It's completely not normal to concede three goals in this kind of game after nine minutes.

"I prepare the team, that is why I am responsible of what's happened on the pitch. I have a lot of work to do because I have to change this kind of thing."

Asked if he will get time to turn Palace's poor form around, he said: "I don't know."

Under his predecessor Oliver Glasner, Palace enjoyed the most successful phase in the club's history, lifting the FA Cup for the first time in 2025 and then winning the Conference League in May.

But Sage has had a tough start at Selhurst Park since he arrived after guiding Lens to the French Cup and second in Ligue 1 last season.

Palace are 14th in the Premier League with two wins from seven games but their 17 goals conceded are the most in the top flight.

"I just want to apologise to the fans," added Sage. "We were not at the level we expected, and I'm really sorry for that because I know how important it is for them, but we didn't show today that it's really important for us too."

Asked on his emotions after the game, he replied: "Only one feeling - shame. When you play this kind of game you have to show another face. It was our worst face."

Palace, with one win and one loss from their two Europa League matches, play on Thursday with a trip to Turkey to take on Besiktas before returning to Premier League action on Sunday at home to Newcastle.

#32. European football: 10-man Lyon hold off Nice to move top of Ligue 1

Five teams level on points after Monaco lose to Lorient

Real Madrid ease past Sevilla with Mbappé double

Ten-man Lyon held on for a 2-1 comeback victory over Nice to move top of Ligue 1 on Sunday, as previous pacesetters Monaco lost for the first time this season. Five teams are level on 14 points at the top of the table with Lyon heading Paris Saint-Germain, Paris FC, Lille and Monaco on goal difference.

It was a close run affair for Lyon, playing in front of local boy and French cycling prodigy Paul Seixas, following Keito Nakamura’s dismissal 20 minutes from time.

Côte d’Ivoire forward Elye Wahi, who opened the scoring for Nice on 18 minutes with his second goal of the season, was denied a stoppage-time equaliser by a tight offside call.

Two goals in three minutes turned the game around by half-time as Pavel Sulc equalised by prodding home a rebound and Tanner Tessmann headed the hosts in front.

Veteran Belgium midfielder Axel Witsel headed against the bar early in the second half while Wahi hit the post with a close-range header, shortly after Nakamura was dismissed for a high boot.

Noah Cadiou’s second-half penalty for Lorient prevented Monaco returning to the top of Ligue 1 as they fell to a 1-0 defeat in Brittany on Sunday.

Finnish goalkeeper Lukas Hradecky dived the right way, but Cadiou placed his spot-kick into the corner, to hand Monaco their first league defeat of the season.

Monaco are one of five teams level on points at the top of the table as they were joined by Paris FC, who edged Rennes 4-3 thanks to Lassine Sinayoko’s injury-time penalty. Rennes dropped to fifth, a point behind, despite forward Estéban Lepaul’s hat-trick of penalties in Paris.

Marseille picked up a much-needed win as they thumped Angers 5-2 to pull away from the relegation zone. Le Havre remain rooted to the foot of the table as Cameroon forward Danny Namaso’s double helped Auxerre come away from Normandy with a 3-1 victory.

Kylian Mbappé scored ⁠twice as Real Madrid closed the gap on ⁠La Liga leaders ⁠Barcelona ​to six points with a 4-1 home win over ⁠Sevilla on Sunday, a week ⁠before the rivals meet in el clásico.

Arda Guler ​opened the ‌scoring in the ‌30th minute, arrowing a shot ‌into the top corner from outside the box, before Mbappé added a second seven minutes later after a brilliant turn. Mbappé ‌then won and converted a penalty in the 63rd minute ​to effectively settle the contest.

Sevilla pulled one back with 10 minutes remaining through the substitute Manu Bueno, ⁠but Yan Diomandé restored Real’s three-goal ​lead ​with a thunderous ​strike two minutes later.

An early penalty from Ante Budimir and a late Asier Osambela goal from earned Osasuna a 2-0 win against Racing Santander while Celta Vigo won 2-1 at home against Alavés.

Ibrahim Maza and Patrik Schick combined to score two goals as Bayer Leverkusen came from behind to beat in-form Freiburg 2-1 in the Bundesliga on Sunday.

After a shock defeat to promoted Elversberg in the season opener, Leverkusen have now picked up 13 of a possible 18 points and sit fourth, level with third-placed Freiburg – who host Bayern Munich next weekend – on points.

Rock bottom Borussia Mönchengladbach are still searching for a first point of the season after losing 2-1 at home against fellow strugglers Hoffenheim.

Hoffenheim’s Bambasé Conté opened the scoring with his second goal in two games since a surprise call-up to the Germany squad in October. Wael Mohya levelled for the hosts just after the break, but Alexander Prass put Hoffenheim back in front shortly afterwards as the visitors, who host Lyon in the Europa League on Thursday, won just their second game of the season.

Lazio’s Danish duo made the difference in Turin as Oliver Provstgaard and Gustav Isaksen ⁠scored in a 3-0 ⁠win over ​Juventus on Sunday that lifted their side level with Inter at the top of Serie A.

Provstgaard broke the deadlock in the ⁠37th minute, using his height to glance home Mattia Zaccagni’s cross after Lazio worked a short corner on the left.

Fellow Dane Isaksen doubled the lead in ⁠the 66th minute, collecting a pass from Nuno Tavares on the right before shifting the ball onto ​his left foot and bending a low ‌finish into the far ‌corner.

Fisayo Dele-Bashiru completed the scoring in the 89th minute, launching a counterattack from inside his own ‌half and driving into the box before slotting home a low finish as frustrated home supporters jeered their side through to the final whistle.

Cesc Fàbregas’s Como ended their three-game winless streak in Serie A on Sunday with a 3-1 victory at lowly Fiorentina.

First-half goals by Mattia Liberali and Nico Paz put the visitors in charge, before Marin Pongracic halved the deficit shortly before the interval. Anastasios Douvikas netted early in the second period to put to bed any hope of a Fiorentina comeback and keep the hosts locked in the relegation zone on four points.

Milan leapfrogged Como into fourth as they survived a second-half comeback from Atalanta to win 3-2. Goals from Gonçalo Ramos, Adrien Rabiot and Mario Gila put Milan 3-0 ahead after 58 minutes before Atalanta rallied through Gianluca Gaetano and Nikola Krstovic.

Earlier, Lecce won 3-0 at Udinese, with Kialonda Gaspar, Konan N’Dri and Jamil Siebert all finding the net.

#36. Michael Carrick says he has blocked out noise surrounding Man United with 'headphones' but believes their draw at Leeds is a 'fresh start' and has 'no doubts' his side can overturn poor run

Published: 20:36 BST, 18 October 2026 | Updated: 20:37 BST, 18 October 2026

Michael Carrick said he needed ‘headphones’ to shut out the noise around Manchester United after a difficult week ended with his team taking a point against Leeds at Elland Road.

Carrick claimed that the 1-1 draw felt like a fresh start for United, but admitted that a run of two wins from 10 games doesn’t look good.

The build-up to the match had been dominated by Lisandro Martinez’s post-match outburst against club bosses in Madrid in midweek, and the Argentina defender only lasted 45 minutes before coming off with a thigh problem.

‘It’s been quiet inside the club but the headphones have been on this week,’ said Carrick.

‘I spoke to the boys this morning about what the game is, the history and what it means to the supporters, to the football club, to us coming over here into their territory and what it takes to win here and get a result.

‘It definitely tests you if you come here and you're not quite there. I take a lot from the way we went about it.

Michael Carrick believes that Man United's 1-1 draw with Leeds is a fresh start for his side

‘We're not getting too carried away because we haven't won the game. But it I felt like a bit of a fresh start, to be honest, in terms of where we're at, and accepting it and doing something about it.’

However, United are still in 13th place in the table with just one Premier League win against newly-promoted Ipswich back in August.

‘I understand the situation doesn't look too good if you look at it from a certain way, but I got no doubts that we can go on a good run,’ added Carrick.

‘Listen, we're not accepting it as everything's great by any stretch, so I'm realistic about that. But sometimes you do struggle.

‘There has been a cycle at times here over a period of time when it can go in different directions. We have got to be stable enough to keep doing the right things as a group.’

Bryan Mbeumo put United ahead in the first half, but Dominic Calvert-Lewin equalised from a corner shortly after half-time as Leeds’ encouraging start to the season continued.

United defender Harry Maguire said: ‘To concede a set-piece after half-time is disappointing. When you come to places like this, you can't be beaten on set plays and we conceded a set play which got them back in the game.

‘We can be better. We have to show more quality with the ball. But you can't question the togetherness, the spirit, the fight. This is a tough place to come. Leeds have been flying in the league.

Dominic Calvert-Lewin's second half equaliser means United only have one win from their seven Premier League matches

‘We got a foothold at about 70 minutes and probably looked the more likely to go and win it, but a draw is probably fair.’

After scoring his fifth goal of the season, Calvert-Lewin said: ‘I just tried to cause a ruckus. I just make it difficult for the defender. I read the flight of the ball and was quickest to react.

‘They are still a very good team with a lot of quality, regardless of the outside noise.’

Leeds boss Daniel Farke was disappointed his team couldn’t take all three points as they produced a good response to their first league defeat of the season at Arsenal.

‘We took it as a compliment that we have done many things right over the last month if we were seen as favourites against Manchester United,’ said Farke. ‘We have earned this and we wanted to prove the comments right.

‘I felt it was not necessary to be losing at half-time, but it is still Manchester United. In the second half, we got the equaliser and we should have kept up the dominance. We should have won the game, but we move on.’

Callum Osmand was on target again as Celtic inflicted more misery on Hearts with a 7-1 thrashing at Parkhead.

Osmand netted twice in two first-half minutes in the first meeting of the teams since his goal sealed Celtic’s last-gasp title success at the expense of the Edinburgh side.

The Hoops were two up inside 10 minutes after Kieran Tierney and Benjamin Nygren both scored from Mika Baur corners, and the latter had the William Hill Premiership champions 5-1 up at the interval after forcing an own goal from Jamie McCart.

Camilo Duran piled on the agony with a goal four minutes after the restart and Nygren rounded off the scoring to send Martin O’Neill’s side four points clear of Rangers.

Hearts had arrived in Glasgow as the division’s top goalscorers and with the opportunity to move two points behind the leaders.

They produced 20 shots at goal, one of which found the net from Laurent Mendy, but Celtic were far superior in the final third and benefited from some extremely slack defending.

Wouter Vrancken’s side were always up against it after the hosts capitalised on Baur’s seventh-minute corner.

The champions recruited set-piece specialist Ross Grant from the Tynecastle coaching team in the summer after Hearts led the way in the league with 23 goals from dead-ball situations. Celtic were in the bottom half of the table with 10.

That emphasis appeared to pay dividends as Liam Scales glanced Baur’s delivery into the goalmouth, where the unmarked Tierney nodded home.

Hearts got first contact on Baur’s next corner but Dane Murray hooked the second ball into the path of Nygren, who cushioned a volley in off a post.

Both sides had chances for the third goal. Home goalkeeper Viljami Sinisalo saved from Sabri Guendouz and Claudio Braga, while McCart’s free header drifted just wide.

Celtic winger Haissem Hassan hit a post and set up Nygren, who was denied by Beau Reus, before Osmand netted his first goal of the season in the 36th minute. Duran set up the 20-year-old to slot home after collecting a slack pass from Guendouz.

Osmand’s second goal came from Duran’s pressing on the halfway line and the Colombian scooped the ball up for the former Fulham player to nod over the line after his own shot was saved.

Some Hearts fans headed for the exit and missed Mendy sweeping the ball into the corner of the net from 20 yards in the 41st minute after being teed up by Josh McPake, who was generally marshalled superbly by Colby Donovan.

Duran came close before Baur rounded off an incredible first half when he ghosted past two players and dinked the ball over Reus. Stephen Kingsley could only knock the ball in off team-mate McCart.

Celtic opened their visitors up again just after the interval when Tierney ran unchallenged to set up Duran to finish first time.

The tempo dipped but the home fans were treated to some virtuoso wing play from half-time substitute Jota before the Magnificent Seven theme tune got another Celtic Park airing in the 83rd minute.

Substitute Kasper Hogh fed the run of Nygren, who finished high into the net.
