#41. Shades of Barca and Beckham - Brighton aim to maintain superb start

Brilliant Brighton put five past struggling Crystal Palace

Not only are Brighton scoring more than everyone else in the Premier League, they are netting better goals too.

Centre-half Lewis Dunk won the Premier League goal of the month award for September with a 35-yard stunner against Coventry. Now, five weeks later, that has already been eclipsed.

Step forward Seagulls team-mate Diego Gomez, who shot from the halfway line having seen Crystal Palace goalkeeper Walter Benitez off his line during Brighton's emphatic 5-0 win over their rivals on Sunday.

Benitez made a rapid dash back to his goal and produced a desperate dive but could not stop the ball going in just under the crossbar.

"As soon as he struck it, I knew it was in. He's taken the club goal of the season off me," joked Brighton skipper Dunk.

"That's the goal of the season so far, what a hit," added former Premier League striker Efan Ekoku, part of the commentary team for BBC Radio 5 Sports Extra. "[It was] superbly struck and right over the head of the keeper from the centre-circle."

Gomez's seventh-minute goal at the Amex put Brighton 2-0 up and was from 51 metres, the furthest long-range Premier League goal since Wayne Rooney scored from 58 metres for Everton in their 4-0 win over West Ham in November 2017.

"When I scored, I didn't know where to run, or what to do," said 23-year-old Paraguay midfielder Gomez. "When I got the ball, I knew the goalkeeper was a little bit ahead. I was very happy with the goal."

Former Newcastle goalkeeper Shay Given, now a Match of the Day pundit, said the goal was "reminiscent of David Beckham [for Manchester United versus Wimbledon in 1996]" and added: "I don't even blame Benitez the goalkeeper.

"We're always talking about sweeper goalkeepers and you've got to be high up for the through ball and the defence playing a high line. I think his position was fine.

"You've just got to take your hat off to Gomez. That is just a brilliant, brilliant goal."

'Why not?' - 'Breathtaking' Brighton in title race says Dublin

Brighton have never finished higher than sixth in English football's top flight, but they now have 16 points from seven matches, with fan hopes rising that they could make a real push for Champions League qualification, or even a title challenge.

Their tally of 23 top-flight goals is four more than league leaders Manchester City, and more than double the 11 of reigning champions Arsenal.

Since the top flight was rebranded as the Premier League in 1992, only three sides have scored more goals across their first seven games of a season - Arsenal in 2009-10 (24), Manchester United in 2011-12 (24), and Manchester City in 2019-20 (27).

In the top five European leagues, only Barcelona, with 39 goals from nine La Liga matches, have more domestic league goals than Brighton.

With 10 different goalscorers, Brighton, third in the table, have also been the great entertainers of the season so far.

They won their opening league game 4-0 against an Aston Villa side that finished fourth in 2025-26, and Fabian Hurzeler's team have shown that was not a one-off. Results since have included winning 5-0 at Coventry, 3-0 against Arsenal, 2-0 at Sunderland despite having a man sent off, and now 5-0 against rivals Palace.

In the Carabao Cup, they fought back from 2-0 down to win 3-2 at Old Trafford and eliminate Manchester United. In Europe, they have justified their position as Conference League favourites, putting four past both Norwegian side Tromso and Lithuanian champions Kauno Zalgiris.

For Hurzeler, the youngest permanent manager in Premier League history when he was appointed in June 2024 at the age of 31, the atmosphere at the Amex could not have been any more different to their previous match with Palace.

When the Eagles won 1-0 in February, Brighton were 14th, had only won one of 12 league games, and the home fans were chanting "you're getting sacked in the morning" at their own boss.

Therefore, it is no surprise that Hurzeler is not getting carried away at his side's good form.

He was quick to shut down any talk that Brighton could be involved in the Premier League title race and said: "We have to stay very humble. The season will be long.

"We have to keep going. We can't be satisfied. We have to keep pushing, stay humble and understand why we are successful at the moment to keep pushing at that level."

The rapid rise of a former art dealer to Europe's hottest young manager

Free-scoring Brighton & Man United settle for a point

Hurzeler was also keen to ensure Gomez remained grounded.

"It's not simple to score a goal like this," added Hurzeler. "Everyone speaks about his goal, but to me the most important thing is the things we can improve, small easy passes we missed.

"It's good to celebrate the win but understand there is still space for improvement especially for individual players.

"We don't train shots from 50 metres. Overall, we know he has a really good finish. In these moments it's about being very precise with his long kick. The perception to recognise the keeper and be quick to go to the action was impressive."

Brighton fans will have to savour the memories of this win and Gomez's goal as all of their next five matches are away from home.

That run includes league games at Liverpool and Manchester City, another trip to Etihad Stadium in the last 16 of the Carabao Cup, as well as Conference League matches in Czech Republic and Spain, against Jablonec and Getafe respectively.

By the time Brighton return to the Amex on 8 November to face Brentford, we will have a better indication of just how optimistic the Seagulls fans can be about their season.

"I know it's rare, but you look at Leicester in 2016 and Blackburn in 1995 when I was a kid," added Given. "At the minute, you'd say they could upset the apple cart, but obviously it's a long winter coming up.

"Being in European competition as well, that will take its toll for sure. But they're having an unbelievable start to the season. Even set-plays as well, they're the best in the league (nine goals scored).

"They've scored the most goals overall and kept the joint-most goals out, so that's a good start for any team to do well, isn't it?!"

#42. James and Carpenter lead Chelsea surge as sorry Spurs hit for six in WSL again

Two goals each from a rampant Lauren James and battling Ellie Carpenter helped Chelsea to cruise past Tottenham and keep the pressure on Manchester City at the top of the Women’s Super League.

It was a thrilling statement from the home team, in a game laden with stunning goals after a first half in which Tottenham more than held their own.

James’s first was cancelled out by Matilda Vinberg approaching half‑time, before Carpenter restored Chelsea’s lead and James added her second. Sjoeke Nüsken and Maika Hamano, on as substitutes, powered in the fourth and fifth before Carpenter completed the rout.

On the impact of her substitutes Sonia Bompastor, the Chelsea head coach, said: “When it happens like that, the fact that they have clarity on what we expect from them, they have clarity on what the team is trying to achieve, and also they are coming with confidence, is always a positive.”

Following Tottenham’s 6-1 defeat by London City Lionesses this month Martin Ho said he was the “most frustrated” he has been during his time at the club. At Stamford Bridge it looked initially like it would be a different story after a strong start, only for the concession of the opening goal to provide a reminder of their defensive issues. Toko Koga was uncharacteristically caught out, the Japan defender being dispossessed by James who drove towards the near post before firing in from the tightest of angles.

The bright play of Ho’s team did not evaporate, though, with Kadeisha Buchanan on hand to steer the ball out for a corner just ahead of Cathinka Tandberg. A deserved equaliser arrived just before the break when Vinberg converted Julie Blakstad’s pinpoint ball towards the far post with a bullet header.

If there was hope that Spurs would end their run of 20 WSL games against big four opposition without a win, enduring 16 defeats in that time, they were crushed in the second half.

“The first 60 minutes, I can take a lot from,” Ho said. “There’s a lot of good performances, a lot of the things we asked, they’ve done in abundance. I couldn’t have asked any more in that first 60 minutes.

Manchester City held off a spirited fightback from Brighton to close out a 3-2 win and maintain their perfect start in the Women’s Super League.

Andree Jeglertz’s side raced into a 3-0 lead after an early double from Khadjia Shaw and a first goal for summer signing Niamh Charles.

Brighton, though, rallied before the break with goals from Olivia Garcia and Caitlin Hayes. City remain two points ahead of Chelsea.

London City Lionesses made it a full house for the top three, beating Everton 2-1. First-half goals from Delphine Cascarino and England winger Freya Godfrey had seemingly put the Lionesses in control.

Everton, though, set up a tense finish after substitute Holly McNamara headed in with 20 minutes left.

Manchester United are up to fifth in the table after a third successive league win, seeing off bottom side Charlton 3-1.

Three goals in the opening quarter of an hour saw Ella Toone and Andrea Medina put United two up before Leah Davidson pulled one back. Julia Zigioitti Olme completed the scoring just after the half-hour mark.

Aston Villa stunned faltering Liverpool, coming from behind to secure a 2-1 win for their first league success of the season. Natalia Ramos scored a spectacular early opener, but Villa improved after half-time, with Chasity Grant firing in an equaliser before a Grace Fisk own goal.

Kelly Gago scored the only goal in the first half as West Ham defeated Crystal Palace 1-0. Press Association

“When you’re on top and you concede that second, the way we conceded, from our possession, then that deflates you maybe as a group a little bit. But we have to recover quickly psychologically.”

It was not so much a Spurs collapse as Chelsea putting their foot on the gas, channelling any anger and frustration felt at a less than dominant first-half performance into one full of gut-busting intensity in the second half. Just before the hour Bompastor’s side retook the lead, when Alyssa Thompson surged into the penalty area from the left before sending an angled cutback for the arriving Carpenter to power in.

No topic is too small or too big for us to cover as we deliver a twice-weekly roundup of the wonderful world of women’s football

Four minutes later James extended their lead, collecting the ball from Lucy Bronze in the centre circle before she powered towards goal, wrongfooted Koga and curled an effort past Lize Kop.

“It’s a big help when you have a player who can create from nothing,” Bompastor said of James. “I’m pleased, but I want to highlight the team performance. When the individuals are performing it’s because the team is performing as well and the players around her are doing the job for her to express her quality on the ball.”

Chelsea’s fourth was equally as stylish; Keira Walsh flicked the ball to Nüsken and she blasted a rising strike home six minutes after coming on.

Hamano found herself in acres of space for the fifth, sending a curling shot into the top corner. Walsh was at fault for Spurs’ late second, waiting too long to receive a pass which Gaupset pounced on and then fired a low effort past Hannah Hampton. Unwilling to let the game finish on a down note, Carpenter swapped the ball from her left foot to her right as she turned and fired in her second.

It was a chaotic finish to an end‑to‑end match, as Chelsea continue to assert their status as serious title contenders.

#46. Where once we had Arsene Wenger's Invincibles, we now endure Mikel Arteta's Unwatchables. Arsenal may have got the job done against Nottingham Forest, but it was scruffy not stylish, writes TOM COLLOMOSSE

Published: 18:25 BST, 18 October 2026 | Updated: 20:09 BST, 18 October 2026

They are Premier League champions and may well retain their title but Arsenal will never set pulses racing outside north London.

Gunners players, coaches and fans will not care and why should they? They waited 22 years to lift the title and if they go back to back, why would any of those supporters worry about how they did it?

This stuff matters, though. Especially this season, which is already in big trouble due to the Manchester City cheating verdict, against which they have appealed.

Fans are disillusioned by the ongoing saga and the wider game needs a spectacular team to celebrate. Sadly, where once we had Arsene Wenger’s Invincibles, we now endure Mikel Arteta’s Unwatchables. One shot on target, one goal, three points. For the second time this season, there were no through-balls. That’s what you get for your £600million starting XI, folks.

Yes, Arsenal’s defending is fabulous, as demonstrated when Declan Rice and Ezri Konsa made goal-saving challenges late on. They do that bit much better than anyone else and you can only admire it.

But for a club who has spent so much on players, where is the spark? Where is the flair? Where is the magic, the wow?

Arsenal leaped back into second in the Premier League after victory over Nottingham Forest

Noni Madueke came off the bench to score an 80th minute winner for the Mikel Arteta's side

It was somehow fitting that their winner from Noni Madueke should take a huge deflection off Forest defender Jair Cunha. Scruffy, not stylish. ‘We showed grit and determination and showed a champion spirit,’ said Madueke. ‘We have the extra belief and mentality.’

In the first half, Arsenal’s best effort was a Gabriel backheel that hit his team-mate Konsa and nearly rolled into the Forest net.

One area you cannot question Arteta is in his use of substitutes. Madueke’s strike made it 24 goal involvements from players off the bench for Arsenal since the start of last season. The five-subs rule is a huge advantage for wealthy clubs with expensive squads but you still need huge skill to make the most of it.

Still though, Arsenal feel like a team reaching success by spreadsheet rather than artistry. The best of Europe, like Bayern Munich, Barcelona and Paris Saint-Germain, thrill with their attacking play. It would be lovely to see Arsenal match that, even sometimes.

They have reportedly hired a creativity guru to bring out-of-the-box thinking to their bid for multiple honours. Perhaps Arteta should ask German Castanos if he can unlock a well-organised defence, as this was beyond his team for much of this encounter.

These are unsettling times for Forest, who competed impressively but are still without a win or a goal at home all season. Oliver Glasner was hired at huge expense in the summer and the start has not been as owner Evangelos Marinakis would have liked. ‘The result feels harsh and unfair,’ said Glasner. ‘In every game we have our moments but we don’t take them.’

Starting the day six points behind Manchester City, Arsenal brought back some of their main men, with Martin Odegaard, Kai Havertz and Bukayo Saka restored to the starting XI while Arteta preferred Eberechi Eze to Madueke on the left. Eze would last only 45 minutes, however.

In the absence of their main creator Morgan Gibbs-White, who did not train all week due to a muscular problem, Forest set up cautiously. Without a league win at the City Ground since April and with only five points on the board, Oliver Glasner could not risk a hiding at home.

Arsenal may have gotten the job done but they have become Mikel Arteta's Unwatchables

In the opening 15 minutes, his team had barely 20 per cent of the ball and completed only 24 passes inside the Arsenal half. Crucially, though, Arsenal were not stretching Glasner’s men.

So carefully are Arsenal’s build-up patterns planned that, at times in the first half, we saw Rice on the right of a back three, and Havertz in the left-back spot. Full-backs Ben White and Riccardo Calafiori stepped into midfield but still Forest stuck to their task.

Midfielder Xaver Schlager was everywhere and at the back, Murillo did not miss a trick. Though often imprecise, Liam Delap did not allow Gabriel or Ezri Konsa a moment’s peace.

Indeed Forest had the first chance as Nico Dominguez, who replaced Gibbs-White, seized on a poor pass from Calafiori. Delap collected Daniel Munoz’s deflected cross and teed up Dan Ndoye for a shot that was tipped around the post. Attempting to meet Neco Williams’ corner, Murillo clashed with Konsa and suffered a cut to his face.

Unable to break through in open play, Arsenal turned to one of last season’s old set-piece favourites. Saka swung over the corner, Calafiori flicked it on and Gabriel backheeled the loose ball goalwards. Luckily for Forest, it hit Konsa and rebounded favourably.

That was about as good as it would be for Arsenal before the break and when Schlager was treated for a head injury, Arteta summoned his players for a mid-match briefing.

Just before the interval, Rice brought down Delap with a clumsy lunge. Williams’ free-kick hit the wall and as players jostled, Bruno Guimaraes hit the deck holding his face. Arsenal ball, danger averted. ‘Are you City in disguise?’ howled the home fans.

It had been desperately poor stuff from the champions though and it was no surprise to see Arteta sprint down the tunnel when referee Michael Oliver blew the half-time whistle.

Right-back Jurrien Timber made a massive impact for the Gunners off the bench

Ineffective again, Eze was hauled off by. Huddled in his training jacket for the second half, Eze appeared lost in thought.

Arteta’s team made just as little impact during the first part of the second half and midway through it, he sent for three more subs. Mikel Merino, Jurrien Timber and Victor Gyokeres were his selections from the £300m worth of talent in reserve, as Havertz, Guimaraes and Ben White made way.

Timber nearly made an immediate impact when he burst into the box from the right and fed the unmarked Rice, whose finish from 15 yards was woeful and did not even test Sels.

Arsenal’s breakthrough arrived when Jair Cunha’s clearance only reached Rice, who transferred it to Madueke. The England winger charged into the box and when his angled effort clipped Cunha’s left thigh, Sels had no chance to stop it.

Forest would have their moments but could not take them. Callum Hudson-Odoi found fellow substitute Chris Wood only for the forward to delay his aim, allowing Rice to race back and make a crucial block. There was still time for Murillo to glide in from the left and beat Rice with an outrageous piece of skill. Instead of the net, though, the Brazilian defender fired into the Trent End and when Konsa blocked another effort from Delap, Arsenal were home.

Nottingham Forest (3-4-2-1): Sels 6; J Cunha 6, Diomande 7, Murillo 7; Munoz 6, McAtee 7, Schlager 7, Williams 6; Ndoye 7 (Kalimuendo 74, 6), Dominguez 7 (Sangare 74, 6); *DELAP 8*.

Arsenal (4-2-3-1): Raya 6; White 5 (Timber 66, 7), Konsa 7, Gabriel 7, Calafiori 6; Rice 7, Guimaraes 6 (Merino 66, 6); Saka 6, Odegaard 6, Eze 5 (Madueke 46, 7); Havertz 5 (Gyokeres 66, 6).

#47. Manchester United miss chance to make statement after turbulent week with draw at Leeds

Please refresh the page or navigate to another page on the site to be automatically logged inPlease refresh your browser to be logged in

Leeds 1-1 Man United: Dominic Calvert-Lewin’s second-half equaliser extended Manchester United’s winless Premier League run to five matches

Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today.

A 1-1 draw at Elland Road in January 2026 for a Manchester United side with a back three and framed by some incendiary comments about Jason Wilcox precipitated the departure of a manager.

A repeat result is less likely to bring the same outcome, not least because Michael Carrick was not the one criticising the director of football. Yet when it seemed Carrick might be turning a corner, that his side were set for their finest result of a stuttering season and that his players were, as he claimed, galvanised by the events of the last week, United lost another lead and the chance to deliver a statement on the pitch.

Compared to the injury-time goals Everton and Tottenham scored, at least there was no late letdown for United – not with Noussair Mazraoui clearing off the line from Anton Stach in the 92nd minute – but they can summon different types of disappointment.

Even as, after adopting Ruben Amorim’s favourite system – probably not a tribute to the Portuguese, even if his valedictory game came against Leeds – they looked more solid in open play, they have now conceded three set-piece goals in Yorkshire already this season, including Dominic Calvert-Lewin’s equaliser. It is a reason why their wait for a Premier League clean sheet goes on.

And, indeed, why their wait for a win does. They have shared the points in their last three top-flight games but, in all competitions, they are without a victory in six matches. Even Amorim never went six without winning, if a triumph on penalties is factored in.

“We are not getting too carried away, because we didn’t win, but if you keep doing the right things for the right reasons you get what you deserve in the end,” said Carrick. “It wasn't a perfect performance, it wasn't our most unbelievable performance, but there was definitely a lot in there that you can show how together the group were. It felt like a fresh start today.” But without the result which would have demonstrated that.

So it did not get worse for Carrick, though there was insufficient evidence to argue it got much better. United had too little threat after conceding. They did not have that much before, either, but at least there was some solidity in a 3-4-3 system, with a back three shielded by twin defensive midfielders.

A half-time lead lent itself to the suggestion their players should criticise Jason Wilcox more often. Two of the players bought by Wilcox combined for the goal. Perhaps, deep in the defence, Lisandro Martinez was celebrating the recruitment he had lamented. But the Argentinian’s eventful week came to an early, and anticlimactic, end as he went off at half-time; if nothing else, that may have spared him the post-match interviews.

United were breached soon after Mazraoui replaced Martinez; even with three centre-backs, none were near Leeds’ likeliest scorer when he got his fourth goal in five games. Calvert-Lewin ran away from Carlos Baleba and held off Bryan Mbeumo when he met Nico Elvedi’s header and hooked in a shot. They had failed to heed the warning from an earlier set-piece from Stach, with Senne Lammens saving Elvedi’s first-half header.

And there was a spirit and a resilience to Leeds, now only beaten in six of their last 32 league matches, and only by champions Arsenal this season. Yet they were below their best. “It says a lot that we are even slightly disappointed with a point against Manchester United,” manager Daniel Farke said. “You always have to be aware, it is still Manchester United. Many, many compliments to my players for a dominant performance against Man United.”

He noted the team that switched shape because of the opposition was in fact United. “It says a lot about how much respect we've earned,” the German said. Carrick only called it a “tweak” but it at least offered indications he can change. His United have floundered against sides with a back three, so he borrowed from Amorim’s infamous fondness for the formation. At times, it seemed United had no centre-forward; at others, it was Mbeumo. Youri Tielemans, signed as a central midfielder, has looked better when others play that role. He was in the front three, and integral in the supply line. “I am really impressed with Youri,” Carrick said.

United led when Mbeumo poked in a shot from Tielemans’ low centre. The same combination had almost brought an earlier breakthrough, with Tielemans’ quality apparent in the inside-right channel as the unmarked Mbeumo headed wide from the Belgian’s cross.

“Bryan gives so much to the team,” said Carrick. With Benjamin Sesko injured, Marcus Rashford unused and Matheus Cunha limited to a cameo, Mbeumo had to. United’s new look was a more defensive one. It still did not lend itself to either a shutout or a victory.

#50. Evanilson swivels his hips to seal Bournemouth win against 10-man Sunderland

Bournemouth’s, and Marco Rose’s, wait for a Premier League win is over. Sunderland, locked in the bottom three, are becoming this season’s object lesson in travelling too far, too fast.

Once Kevin Danso was dismissed in the 17th minute for the denial of a goalscoring opportunity, Sunderland were sunk. If Evanilson was the match-winner with a goal, an assist and as the player Danso fouled, Régis Le Bris’s team were architects of their own downfall. “A bad day, a bad start,” the Sunderland manager said. Sixth and seventh last season, both teams have struggled domestically while cruising in the Europa League but Sunderland’s troubles deepened.

There was mitigation on offer. With a tight turnaround from Leiria on Thursday, England’s south coast on Sunday and Poznan in midweek, Wearside resources are stretched and their European dream comes against uncomfortable domestic realities. Talk of a possible sale continues, a boardroom reshuffle placing Kyril Louis-Dreyfus, the youthful majority owner, in charge of day‑to‑day operations. On the pitch, Sunderland have not had a league win since August, and lost four in succession.

Both teams had made five changes from Thursday and Bournemouth, who had beaten Sturm Graz at home, were visibly fresher. “Fatigue for me is not an issue,” Le Bris said. “We just have to get used to it.”

Granit Xhaka’s early stumble prefaced a jet-lagged, error-strewn performance that followed Sunderland’s first European away game since 1973. After Lewis Cook dabbed the ball forward, Evanilson seized on a collective muddle between Danso and Omar Alderete. The Brazilian’s reputation for unselfishness was deepened by his next choice of action. Instead of shooting, he laid up a diving Marcus Tavernier to head home. “I was waiting for him to shoot but he can see more than you and me,” Rose said.

“Exactly the situation we wanted to avoid,” Le Bris said, and Danso’s exit swiftly made things worse. Evanilson again escaped beyond a dallying defender exposed by Alderete ducking away from the ball. Clumsiness served as no defence. Craig Pawson, the referee, could reach no decision other than sending the Austrian for an early sachet of shower gel.

Being a goal and a man up represented a challenge to Bournemouth; they had previously conceded nine points from winning positions. First‑half chances piled up, Robin Roefs repeatedly asked to bail out bungling defenders. “If you have one player more you have to use the momentum,” Rose said.

With pressure piling on, the season lurching, Le Bris can only fight with the players available. Brian Brobbey, on the bench in Portugal following injury on international duty, was missing altogether from the matchday squad. “We decided not to rush the process,” Le Bris said. Timur Tutierov, loaned last season to Exeter, chased autumnal shadows before a merciful substitution on 59 minutes.

On the sidelines Rose, who revealed last week that he had binge‑watched Sunderland ’Til I Die on Netflix, kicked every ball. His need for three points was implicit. With the Vitality Stadium modernising fast, fans sitting in new-build corner stands, relegation battles cannot be countenanced. The second goal was accompanied by a collective sigh of relief, arriving via more Sunderland benevolence. Evanilson, assisted by Alderete’s brain-fog backpass, supplied a hip swivel of which Rudolf Nureyev might have been proud, sitting Roefs down to slot into an empty net. “I am happy that he rewarded himself with a goal,” Rose said of his No 9. “He is always working hard for the team.”

Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football

Bournemouth signed off with 29 shots. If thoughts understandably drifted to Thursday and Milan, seven-time European champions, coming to Dorset, Rose would not allow his players to be distracted. Though Sunderland enjoyed a late, brief spell of pressure, Bournemouth calmly collected a win that capped a historic week in club history. “It felt very clear, after [the 5-1 defeat on Friday against] Chelsea we were waiting for this game,” Rose said. “I am settling in well, I love the region. It’s a pleasure to work here. Everyone here stays patient and I really appreciate it.”

For Le Bris, any European success will only be a sticking plaster. “It’s hard to fix without a specific pattern,” he said, lamenting many mistakes. “It wasn’t the best version of Sunderland.”

Two clubs facing similar challenges appear on different trajectories.

#56. Under-fire Crystal Palace boss Pierre Sage could become first Premier League managerial sacking this season after 5-0 thrashing at bitter rivals Brighton - with club chiefs concerned about his defensive tactics

Published: 19:39 BST, 18 October 2026 | Updated: 19:40 BST, 18 October 2026

Pierre Sage is under growing pressure at Crystal Palace and could become the first Premier League manager sacked this season after an embarrassing 5-0 defeat against rivals Brighton.

Palace chiefs have raised concerns about Sage’s defensive approach for several weeks and considered sacking him in September but a goalless draw against Leeds bought him more time.

However, the backline continues to ring alarm bells at Selhurst Park, leaving Sage’s position at risk.

Palace have the worst defensive record in the league, conceding 17 goals in seven Premier League games.

The French coach is also understood to have a strained relationship with key decision-makers, who doubt his defensive methods.

The Daily Mail previously reported that his decision to bench Jaydee Canvot after a bad game irked chairman Steve Parish.

Pierre Sage said he didn't know how long he would be given to turn things round at Palace

Speaking after Palace’s 5-0 defeat at Brighton, Sage was unsure whether he would be given more time in the job.

‘I don’t know,’ Sage said when asked if he would keep his job. ‘I just want to apologise to the fans because it’s not normal to show this face for this club against this other club and we are not at the level we expected.

‘I am really sorry for that because I know how important it is for them. We didn’t show that today. It was really important for us too. We didn’t understand in which context this game was played.

‘I will always give my best. When we lose, I’m really frustrated, but I always take the lesson and try to change things. But it’s the same when I win because I know we can improve.

‘I don’t want to accept the level of the moment if we can do better. Today the work is really important to do and I will do it. It’s my job and I like to change this kind of thing.’

#57. Harry Maguire says Manchester United lack ‘bravery’ after Leeds draw eases pressure on Michael Carrick

Please refresh the page or navigate to another page on the site to be automatically logged inPlease refresh your browser to be logged in

The defender praised tactical tweaks but highlighted one flaw in an improved performance at Elland Road

Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today.

Harry Maguire has suggested that Manchester United must show more bravery despite digging deep to take a point from Elland Road, with the centre-back hailing Michael Carrick’s tweak of formation for a more resolute defensive performance.

Bryan Mbeumo had given the visitors a first-half lead before Leeds marksman Dominic Calvert-Lewin levelled early in the second period of a high-intensity encounter.

While Carrick’s team may be disappointed for squandering their first half-time lead of the campaign, it was a far more convincing performance at the end of a troubling week.

Manchester United lined up with no recognised centre-forward as a midfield of Andrey Santos, Carlos Baleba and Youri Tielemans did well to stifle their hosts.

“We worked on it this week,” Maguire told Sky Sports of the change. “We wanted to match them up without the ball and go quite aggressive. We knew we could get a lot of joy in the middle of the pitch with them only playing two in there.”

However the defender also thought that his team lacked the courage to really kick on at a ground where they have not lost for 24 years.

He added: “That's probably the area of the game where we could have done more. We could have been a bit braver with the ball and taken the ball under pressure.

“But we're in a circumstance where we are not as brave as we should be, and we have to get that back because to win games for Manchester United we have to have that bravery and composure.”

Having lost away to Atletico Madrid in the Champions League on Tuesday, a point brought under-pressure Carrick some respite.

Lisandro Martinez remained in the starting XI after his outburst at transfer chief Jason Wilcox, which later led to an apology, before coming off at the interval with a knock.

Carrick, whose side now travel to Como for another European tie on Wednesday, described the Elland Road encounter as a “tough game” but added: “Not getting too carried away because we didn’t win the game. It felt like a fresh start… the boys are desperate to do well.”

Daniel Farke, the Leeds head coach, described himself as “slightly disappointed” not to win, believing that his team should have kicked on once level. They sit seventh in the standings.

“We should have kept up the dominance, too many strikes went over the crossbar but it was overall a solid performance. We should have won the game but we move on,” he said.

#58. Neville delivers Carrick warning after Man Utd 'stepping stone' performance

Man Utd's winless run stretched to six games as Dominic Calvert-Lewin's second-half strike from a corner cancelled out Bryan Mbeumo's opener to leave Michael Carrick's side in 13th after claiming just one win in their first seven Premier League matches this season

Football Expert & Columnist @GNev2

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player

Sky Sports pundit Gary Neville believes Manchester United's 1-1 draw at Leeds could be a "stepping stone" but has warned that Michael Carrick will have a problem if his side are still 13th in the Premier League come January.

United have just seven points from seven league matches, winning just one of those, which is their fewest number of victories at this stage of a top-flight season for 40 years.

Despite extending their winless run in all competitions to six games with the draw at Elland Road, the performance was much improved, with Carrick's tactical tweaks making his side more compact and defensively solid.

Neville agreed with the United head coach's assessment that Sunday's performance at Elland Road was a step in the right direction.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player

Speaking on the Gary Neville podcast, the Sky Sports pundit said: "[There's] a depressed standard and a low expectation right now.

"But it'll feel like a stepping stone for Michael Carrick, and it'll feel like the first step on the ladder in the Premier League.

"They may take some confidence from that, and there might be a blueprint there. Maybe we have to bring Matheus Cunha, Marcus Rashford and others off the bench, and we might just have to have a go at being more solid."

United's paltry points return has them sitting 13th in the Premier League after seven games, already five points adrift of fifth place, which was enough for Champions League qualification last season.

Neville says there is no need for panic just yet but feels United have to show signs of improvement over the next few weeks otherwise Carrick could find himself in hot water come the new year.

"I would say fourth would be a birdie, fifth would be par, and sixth would be a bogey," said Neville of his former club's targets for the season. "But they can't finish outside the top five, because then you're missing out on Champions League and it becomes a vicious circle.

"Then you can't get those players because they want to play in the Champions League and you can't get the money from it and you've lost the £60m-£70m and you're in the Europa League on Thursday nights.

"Fifth is a must for Michael Carrick to continue to grow and Manchester United continue to grow with investment.

"If they're 13th in January, he's got a problem because then you are what you are. Whereas I think it's still early enough, seven points from seven games, to say, 'okay, still early in the season'. You can't say that after 15 games.

"It has to change in the next few weeks: Bournemouth is really important and Chelsea away. And how he manages the games in between that.

"You've got to say fifth. You know that anything less than fifth is going to be a disappointment and a dropping standard from the start of the season where everybody expected them to finish.

"And at the moment, they're well short of that because you look at Brighton, Liverpool, Aston Villa - they look like they're picking up a little bit. It's difficult."

Neville has seen encouraging signs from Carlos Baleba's start to life as a Manchester United player and feels the midfielder staying fit is crucial for Carrick this season.

Signed from Brighton for £70m at the end of the summer window, the 21-year-old arrived with an ankle injury that has kept him from featuring until he came on in the second half of last Saturday's 1-1 draw against 10-man Tottenham.

Baleba has started the last two games, at Atletico Madrid and Leeds, and brought an added steel to United's midfield alongside fellow summer-signing Andrey Santos.

"I know he had a difficult season last year at Brighton, but you watch him in his first couple of games or so for United, and he's got something," said Neville. "He's got a bit of strength about him, he's got a presence.

"Him staying fit is gonna be absolutely critical, I can understand why Michael Carrick took him off with 20 minutes to go [at Leeds], because he's played [nearly] three games in a week.

"Maybe he doesn't play him against Como on Wednesday. We're not throwing the Champions League away, but Manchester United have to beat Bournemouth next weekend.

"I just wonder whether that Santos-Baleba partnership is going to stay there for a bit, and let a couple of [the attacking players] float around in front, and be a lot more solid, make sure we're not giving as much space away.

"I'm sick of Manchester United's team being easy to play against, and Michael Carrick will be sick of it."

Celtic move four points clear of Rangers after win

Rangers held to pulsating 2-2 draw against Dundee

Callum Osmand was on target again as Celtic inflicted more misery on Hearts with a 7-1 thrashing at Parkhead.

Osmand netted twice in three first-half minutes in the first meeting of the teams since his goal sealed Celtic’s last-gasp title success at the expense of the Edinburgh side.

The Hoops were two up inside 10 minutes after Kieran Tierney and Benjamin Nygren both scored from Mika Baur corners, and the latter had the Premiership champions 5-1 up at the interval after forcing an own goal from Jamie McCart.

Camilo Durán piled on the agony with a goal four minutes after the restart and Nygren rounded off the scoring to send Martin O’Neill’s side four points clear of Rangers.

Hearts had arrived in Glasgow as the division’s top goalscorers and with the opportunity to move two points behind the leaders.

They produced 20 shots at goal, one of which found the net from Laurent Mendy, but Celtic were far superior in the final third and benefited from some extremely slack defending.

Rangers passed up the chance to go top of the Premiership in a pulsating 2-2 draw against Dundee at Dens Park on Saturday. The home side took a deserved lead in the 38th minute through the striker Bradley Fink but the returning Gers attacker Badredine Bouanani fired in a stunning equaliser three minutes later with his first goal for the club.

Derek McInnes’s side came out re-energised for the second half and took the lead on the hour with the midfielder Nico Raskin’s long-range drive but in the 68th minute the midfielder Callum Jones took advantage of Gers slackness to level. Dundee were well worth a point.

Greg Kiltie scored twice to lift Kilmarnock off the bottom with a 3-2 home victory over Motherwell. Kiltie struck first and last as Neil McCann’s side inflicted a fifth consecutive defeat on the Steelmen, who join Killie in the bottom three, one point above bottom-placed Hibernian.

Motherwell had a dominant spell after recovering from Kiltie’s second-minute opener and goals from Alex Lowry and Seb Palmer-Houlden turned the game on its head. But Tyreece John-Jules soon equalised and Motherwell were cut open before Kiltie knocked home a 69th-minute winner.

Motherwell’s manager, Alfred Johansson, bemoaned his side’s defending, saying: “I’m very, very disappointed and frustrated with how we end this game. It’s extremely difficult to accept the fact that we lost this game. We have chances to score more than two goals but we can’t rely on scoring three goals away from home. We need to be much more solid. It’s just way too low a level, how we defend.”

Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football

Falkirk secured an entertaining 2-1 win at Hibernian. Their only other league victory this term was at home to Hearts in September.

In a game that went from end to end, Jacob Murrell put Falkirk 2-0 ahead inside 37 minutes, before Hibs struck back with an Owen Elding goal. The home side dominated the second half, but could not bag an equaliser.

Aberdeen returned to winning ways as a 3-1 victory over St Mirren moved them above their opponents, who have now lost five straight matches. Brad Lyons gave the hosts the lead in spectacular fashion after two minutes, but the Buddies went on to dominate the first half and levelled through Eseosa Sule. In a much-improved second-half display strikes from Kevin Nisbet and Ayoub Mouloua gave the Dons three points. Aberdeen are seventh.

Lyall Cameron’s 79th-minute strike earned Dundee United a 1-1 draw at St Johnstone. United trailed at half-time to a Josh Fowler goal, the striker’s sixth of the Premiership campaign. The league’s top scorer did not make it out for the second half due to illness and Simo Valakari’s side were unable to repeat the trick of last Sunday in Aberdeen when they successfully defended a 1-0 lead.

Jim Goodwin had too many creative and attacking options to throw at their hosts and despite a decent defensive stand from the hosts, Cameron struck the second goal of his impressive loan spell from Rangers. The clubs are locked together on 12 points in the top half of the table after encouraging starts to the campaign, with the Saints in fifth on goal difference.

Bournemouth have set a new club record Premier League attendance of 12,004 at the Vitality Stadium. The record was set during Sunday’s win against Sunderland.

The northwest and southeast corners of the stadium opened for the first time on Thursday night. That occasion saw the Cherries beat Austrian side Sturm Graz 3-0 in the Europa League.

The Sturm Graz fixture was the first European home game at the south coast ground. The stadium has grown in capacity with the addition of the new seating, part of an ongoing revitalisation project.

Writing in the programme, Cherries chief Jim Frevola said: “It has been great to see the two corners open and supporters enjoying the additional space and improved facilities, even though there are still some finishing touches and outstanding items for us to address.

“Behind the South Stand, the enabling works and piling operations are continuing. While much of the work takes place away from the immediate matchday experience, it is essential to delivering our longer-term ambitions for the stadium.

“I am excited about what lies ahead. We know there is still plenty to do, but each stage brings us closer to creating a stadium that better serves our supporters, our players and the wider club.”

The new corners brought additional space and improved facilities for supporters, according to Mr Frevola, who also noted that finishing touches and outstanding items remain to be addressed.

#69. Arsenal win with one shot on target as Forest sink into bottom three

Nottingham Forest vs Arsenal. Premier League.

Report and free match highlights as Noni Madueke’s deflected winner earned Arsenal a hard-fought victory at Nottingham Forest; the Gunners stay within three points of Premier League leaders Manchester City, while Forest drop into the relegation zone

Football Journalist @williambitibiri

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player

Arsenal's only shot on target proved enough to snatch victory at Nottingham Forest through Noni Madueke's deflected strike, keeping the champions within touching distance of Premier League leaders Manchester City and condemning Forest to the relegation zone.

After 80 frustrating minutes at the City Ground, substitute Madueke cut inside from the left and fired towards goal. His strike deflected off Jair Cunha, wrong-footed Matz Sels and found the net to settle a game in which Arsenal had struggled to turn possession into chances.

Arsenal had dominated the ball but registered no shots on target in the first half. Kai Havertz headed wide from a Declan Rice free-kick while Gabriel's set-piece effort was cleared almost off the line by Ousmane Diomande.

Forest made life difficult for Mikel Arteta's side, defending resolutely and threatening on the counter. Murillo almost salvaged a point in stoppage time with a superb solo run, driving at the Arsenal defence before curling narrowly wide. Ezri Konsa then made a crucial late challenge to deny Liam Delap.

However, despite their opportunities, it was the same old story for Oliver Glasner's side, who failed to find a breakthrough.

The result takes Arsenal to 18 points, three behind leaders Manchester City. For Forest, the frustration deepens. They drop into the relegation zone and are still waiting for their first home league goal of the season.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player

Analysis by Sky Sports' William Bitibiri:

Eberechi Eze has spent a year at Arsenal since leaving Crystal Palace, but questions remain over whether he is ready to become one of the club's leading figures as their ambitions continue to grow.

His talent is undeniable. The real concern is whether he can influence games consistently, and the trip to Nottingham Forest presented another opportunity to silence his doubters.

With Arsenal struggling to break down Forest, Eze had the chance to make a difference. Instead, he was substituted at half-time, watching from the sidelines as Noni Madueke replaced him and went on to score the 80th-minute winner.

Roy Keane's assessment on Sky Sports was telling, suggesting his concerns extended beyond a single performance.

"We're still waiting for him, the talent is there," Keane said. "We just want him to be at Arsenal and be able to take responsibility and try to be the main man at a big club."

That is the challenge facing Eze. At Crystal Palace, he was the focal point, the player expected to create chances and turn games in his team's favour. At Arsenal, however, talent alone will not earn him that status. He must deliver consistently, particularly in tight contests when his team need inspiration.

Ian Wright offered some important context, describing Eze as a "moments player" who benefits from having players around him and can become isolated on the left.

There is merit to that argument. Eze offers a different threat to Madueke, whose pace, directness and willingness to take on defenders gave Arsenal a fresh dimension in the second half.

Yet that only underlines the challenge facing the former Palace man. While Madueke seized his opportunity and made an immediate impact, Eze failed to leave his mark on the contest.

Competition for places is healthy at a club with Arsenal's ambitions. For Eze, though, the task is no longer simply to showcase his ability in flashes. He must demonstrate that he can influence games regularly, take responsibility when his team need him and establish himself as a first-choice player.

The talent is there. Now, Eze must prove he can turn that potential into consistent performances and become one of Arsenal's main men.

Analysis by Sky Sports' William Bitibiri:

There was only so long Nottingham Forest could rely on defensive resilience before their lack of goals caught up with them. Now they are in the relegation zone.

Oliver Glasner's side have failed to score in every Premier League home game this season, and their defeat to Arsenal highlighted why they are in trouble.

Forest competed and created opportunities, but lacked the quality in the final third to make their efforts count.

Liam Delap struggled to make an impact against Arsenal's defence, summing up a frustrating afternoon. Forest needed someone to take responsibility, but their attacking play lacked conviction.

That is the worry for Glasner. Defensive organisation can only take a team so far; they still need goals to win matches.

Forest are now in the relegation zone with just five points. Their performances offer some encouragement, but until they find a reliable source of goals at the City Ground, it is difficult to see their situation improving.

"We also had our moments and it's important when you play the champions you take your moments.

"But today, the performance, effort, spirit and energy we had was on a very good level. But the result is frustrating."

#71. 'Maybe we became arrogant' - Sunderland struggles continue

Bournemouth pick up first league victory with win over Sunderland

Nordi Mukiele offered a brutally honest verdict about why Sunderland have struggled so far this season, following their impressive return to the Premier League last term.

The Black Cats defender had his say after a 2-0 defeat by Bournemouth on Sunday. It was Sunderland's fourth Premier League loss in a row and leaves them second bottom in the table.

Only those inside the club can answer Mukiele's "arrogant" claim after the Black Cats' drop-off in results and performance.

They surprised everyone last season by qualifying for the Europa League at the first time of asking after eight years away from the top flight.

But have Sunderland been found out by their rivals? Are they suffering the somewhat mythical second season syndrome? Or might they simply be struggling with the added demands of European football?

"I think this game is just what we are looking [like] from the beginning of the season," Mukiele told Sky Sports. "We are not good enough.

"Why? I don't know. Maybe because we became arrogant, this is what I think."

Sunderland head coach Regis le Bris was not quite as damning but still disappointed.

"We were below the level, it's really clear. It's hard to take, hard to digest," Le Bris told Sky Sports.

"It's very painful because we were not Sunderland and it's not acceptable."

Danso was sent off in Sunderland's defeat against Bournemouth

After seven games last season, Sunderland had 11 points and were ninth in the table having won three, drawn two and lost two.

At the same point this term, they have four points with one win, a draw and five defeats.

"We won't find excuses," said Le Bris. "We have a busy schedule. We want to embrace the challenge, but the position at the minute is not good."

Sunderland's league form so far points to a relegation battle, but in Europe they have a 100% record after wins over Dutch side AZ Alkmaar and second-tier Portuguese outfit Torreense.

They have now lost both games in the immediate aftermath of their Europa League outings, although one of those was an eight-goal thriller against unbeaten league leaders Manchester City.

Former Newcastle United goalkeeper Shay Given â who had a loan spell at Sunderland in 1996 while a Blackburn Rovers player â believes the Black Cats' squad may be not sufficiently set up to deal with the extra games after last season's seventh-placed finish.

He does see a route out of relegation danger, though.

"They overachieved last season, getting into European competition," said Given.

"I don't know if the squad is ready for a challenge on all fronts. You need a bigger squad, a deeper squad, and it's going to be a big ask. I'm just looking at the table and they're second bottom at the minute.

"I know it's only seven games played, but there are so many games coming up and in a short period of time. It's about the bread and butter in the Premier League - that's the most important thing. You like to think with Le Bris, they'll have enough to be safe."

Sunderland spent Â£161m on 15 new players after gaining promotion to the Premier League in the summer of 2025.

In the transfer window this summer, they invested about Â£60m on five new recruits but their success was probably more in keeping key players such as captain Granit Xhaka and striker Brian Brobbey, who is currently out with a hamstring injury.

Xhaka calls for calm following fifth Premier League defeat

Whether or not Sunderland's squad is deep enough, heading to Bournemouth to face a side who were without a league win before Sunday and had also just played in Europe on Thursday should have been one they were relishing.

Yet Sunderland could not have made it easier for the hosts at Vitality Stadium.

One of the recent summer recruits, Kevin Danso â a loan signing from Tottenham Hotspur - was bullied by Evanilson in the build-up to Marcus Tavernier's opener in just the sixth minute.

Centre-back Danso was then sent off in the 17th minute for dragging down the Brazilian striker when he was clear through on goal.

In the second half, Omar Alderete's weak backpass to goalkeeper Robin Roefs gifted Evanilson the chance to secure the three points for the Cherries.

According to Opta, in the Premier League this season no side has committed more errors leading to goals than Sunderland with five.

Alderete also became just the third player to commit multiple errors leading to goals this season, alongside team-mate Danso and Hull's Konstantinos Tzolakis.

Sunderland have also conceded 14 goals - only Crystal Palace and Ipswich Town have shipped more - which is more than double their goals-against tally after seven games last season.

They have only scored six, and their three attempted shots in Sunday's game â all off target - represented the lowest total for any team in a Premier League match this season.

It should be noted they have faced Manchester City, champions Arsenal and in-form Brighton, so it has not been an easy start.

"It's just the beginning. Football is like this," said Mukiele. "You can accept and just stand up and go back to work. If I believe we can go back to the top again, yeah, I believe about this.

"It depends about what we really want and this starts in training because we don't do enough and after you can see it on the pitch.

"You cannot lie about football and today I don't want to say we didn't want to win this game, but it didn't look like we want something.

"We just have to work hard to be back where we were like last season because right now this is not us - this is not Sunderland."

#72. Martínez back ‘in a few weeks’ after jaw surgery; Liverpool lose Szoboszlai for ‘some time’ – matchday live

All the latest on Sunday as there was positive news for Chelsea’s goalkeeper after surgery and bad news for Liverpool

Chelsea goalkeeper Emiliano Martínez said he would be fit to return “in a few weeks” following surgery on a fractured jaw sustained during his team’s 2-0 Premier League win at Everton.

The Argentina international was taken to hospital after colliding with Everton defender Jarrad Branthwaite during the second half of Saturday’s game at Hill Dickinson Stadium. Martínez, 34, required eight minutes of treatment on the pitch before he was carried off on a stretcher. Chelsea boss Xabi Alonso later said he had suffered a concussion.

“Thanks to everyone for the messages. The operation went well,” Martínez wrote on social media on Sunday alongside a photo of himself in a hospital bed. “The most important thing is that we won, and kept a clean sheet. We’ll be back in a few weeks.”

Mike Penders is set to deputise in Martínez’s absence. The 21-year-old made his Premier League debut as a substitute against Everton. He joined from Belgian club Genk in August 2024 and has spent the past two seasons out on loan, including a spell at Strasbourg last term.

“The perception of me is that, basically, I am a madman,” James McClean says calmly. “I’m outspoken. I’m a loudmouth. I’m very opinionated and I hate all things British. That’s from people who don’t know me. The reality is quite the opposite. I’m pretty boring. I go training, go home and switch off. A lot of my days are quite bland, quite basic.”

McClean sounds as sane as he looks gaunt on a bleak Monday in Derry. He spent 14 years in English football and the fact that he is now at war with his own club, Derry City, can’t obscure the fact that he is the fifth-most-capped Republic of Ireland international, having played 103 times. “People define success in different ways,” he says, “but I’m the only footballer from the north of Ireland to win over 100 caps for Ireland. I played 150 Premier League games over five seasons, 800 professional games and won a lot of individual accolades. I count that as success and don’t look back with regrets.”

But there’s sadness, too, in the way his life and career were scarred by his refusal to wear the poppy when playing games around Remembrance Sunday in England. “It’s completely changed me as a person,” McClean says. “It’s made me a bit of a recluse because I don’t trust a lot of people now. I’ve been stung bad.”

McClean’s autobiography, The Walls, is one of the best sports books of the year. It’s a powerful and sometimes disturbing read elevated by McClean’s willingness to show himself in an unflattering light.

From the archive: Leeds United v Man Utd classics

double quotation markLeeds United 1-0 Manchester United (FA Cup semi-final replay, 31 March 1965); Leeds United 0-1 Manchester United (Division One, 17 April 1965)

Here’s where the stags really begin to rut. Don Revie’s side, freshly promoted, were on course for the Double. Only problem was, so were Matt Busby’s men. The pair were drawn in the semi-final of the FA Cup, and spent 90 minutes at Hillsborough kicking seven colours out of each other, Jack Charlton, Billy Bremner, Nobby Stiles, Denis Law and Paddy Crerand enjoying themselves like the proverbial pigs. Good luck if you found yourself in the middle of that.

Brouhahas broke out on the terraces as well, and did so again four days later during the replay at the City Ground. The on-field behaviour was much improved, though. According to Big Jack, Manchester United put on a performance as stylish and dangerous as they ever were under Busby, but Leeds somehow held on, wrested the ascendency, and nicked it in the last minute, Bremner twisting in mid-air to steer home an outrageous curling header.

Bremner was missing 18 days later when Manchester United came to Elland Road in the league. Had they won, Leeds would have gone five clear at the top with four games left. They went into the game as favourites, Busby’s side having failed to find the net against Leeds in both Cup games and the earlier league match at Old Trafford, which the visitors won 1-0. That particular lean spell ended after 14 minutes – or 284, if you like – when John Connelly drove home. Leeds failed to respond, despite the best efforts of the newly crowned Football Writers’ player of the year, Bobby Collins, and went down again in their next Bremner-less match, a 3-0 hosing at Sheffield Wednesday. Busby’s third great side won their first title; Revie’s team, not quite ready yet, lost the Cup final as well.

The first time Fernando Roig watched Villarreal play as their president, he sat in the stand at a tiny whitewashed ground that had concrete fever and was half empty. It was a Sunday night in the second division, they lost 3-0 to Badajoz, and he didn’t enjoy it much.

But then, he doesn’t ever enjoy it much. Even on Tuesday at Anfield, he will not: into his 30th year, the longest presidency in Europe, that is about the only thing that hasn’t changed. More than 1,000 games and still it happens. “I don’t get nervous. It’s worse: I get worried, very anxious,” he says. “I suffer a lot.

“It’s emotional to play Liverpool. This will be the fifth time we have faced them, the third at Anfield. The other two were European semi-finals. I’ll watch the morning training session, travel with the team. We’ll go and eat; everywhere we go we get treated very well and we treat them well back. The next day I’ll watch the under-19s in the morning, that I do like. And then the game, which I don’t. Then we’ll fly back here very, very late. It’s very stressful.”

If the 2013 FA Cup final represented a blip for the Sheikh Mansour-era Manchester City in their quest for total domination of English football, it was a historic moment for their conquerors, Wigan Athletic. Memories of that famous day at Wembley still endure for Latics’ supporters despite the relegation from the Premier League that followed. Yet watching the modern-day Wigan, who remain bottom of League One despite a 1-0 win over Reading on Saturday, makes the toppling of City in a Cup final seem an epoch ago.

The club, perhaps understandably, continue to hark back to their halcyon days. Last season they brought back Gary Caldwell – club captain in 2013 – for his second stint as manager, having led the club to promotion from this division in 2015-16. Choosing to swap Exeter for a return to the Latics last season was seen as a risky move by Caldwell, considering the shoestring budget imposed upon him by Mike Danson, the owner who is keen to sell.

Finances are ultra-tight at the Greater Manchester club amid dwindling crowds and losses on the pitch and on the balance sheet. The local businessman Danson and his family saved Wigan from liquidation in June 2023 after mismanagement from previous owners brought a points deduction and relegation from the Championship. Three successive mid-table finishes in League One under their stewardship have brought a semblance of stability, but this season they have plummeted.

The problem is the Dansons have been unable to find an ambitious buyer to take the club to the next level. Now the prospect of a first season in the fourth tier since 1996-97 is a distinct possibility, although victory against Reading – the Latics’ second league win of the campaign, sealed by Scott Hogan’s 71st-minute strike – made the picture a little rosier.

Manchester United travel to old rivals Leeds with pressure mounting on Michael Carrick. United are off to their worst league start in 40 years and were plunged further into chaos by the defender Lisandro Martínez’s attack on the club’s hierarchy over a lack of investment in the squad after Tuesday’s 2-0 defeat by Atlético Madrid. The Argentinian pulled no punches despite being one of those most culpable for a miserable start to the campaign for his part in goals conceded to Fulham and Tottenham in recent weeks. United have won just one of their opening six league games and were also dumped out of the League Cup by Brighton. Leeds last beat the Red Devils at Elland Road back in 2002, but did inflict the only home defeat of Carrick’s interim spell in charge last season when the sides met in April. There is no love lost in this footballing War of the Roses and Michael Butler dons heavy armour at the helm of our live blog while Jamie Jackson and Barney Ronay will file reports and analysis.

Boos accompanied the final whistle at the Emirates Stadium, as the result left Arsenal on six points from six matches and without a win in five Women’s Super League matches, the club’s longest winless run in WSL history. Alessia Russo had hit the woodwork in the first half with a diving header, among a slew of Arsenal chances as Sophie Baggaley was kept the busier of the goalkeepers.

The sun shone. The temperature was in the high 20s. There was a mood of great conviviality. If you were struggling with the official allocation, it turned out you could just email the president of Torreense and he’d sort you out. Were these “Nuno-tickets” real? It turned out they were. Not only that, but you could sit anywhere you wanted in a stadium too big for the game and, if you happened to have gravitated to the comfortable hospitality seating at the back of the lower tier, the beer was inexplicably free.

Locals in Leiria seemed bewildered but could hardly have been more accommodating. A beer pump had been installed outside a patisserie on the Praça Francisco Rodrigues Lobo, whose owner soon found fans happy to help stack empty barrels if that facilitated the free flow of Sagres. “There was a meeting at the town hall to explain these are not hooligans,” said the owner of a radical leftist flammkuchen restaurant between the square and the cathedral. “They told us the club comes from the labour movement and I found that very interesting.” And how had she found the fans? “Noisy, but with a quirky sense of humour.”

This was everything Sunderland fans could have wished for from their first European away game in 53 years and more. They had seen other fans experience these things, and now they could tick off the checklist: complicated travel to a pretty foreign town they would otherwise never visit, a fussy Albanian referee and a great sense of togetherness and community. There was even an injury-time winner from, miracle of miracles, Noah Sadiki.

Ask any of the 5,000 or so Wearsiders who made the trip to Portugal if the Europa League was worth it and the answer would be unanimous. Bournemouth, Crystal Palace and Brighton fans would surely say something similar: European football, especially for clubs who are unfamiliar with it, is a joy and an adventure. It generates experiences that will be remembered for ever, and if the cost is that the risk of relegation goes up, that’s a price worth paying. Others at those clubs may see things differently.

Spurs’ bright start to the campaign ended before the international break thanks to a 6-1 drubbing by London City Lionesses. By contrast, their London rivals are on a roll under Sonia Bompastor, unbeaten in 13 WSL games and with four wins on the spin. Six consecutive clean sheets in all competitions – their longest such run since December 2021 – underline the Blues’ glowing form. Chelsea goalkeeper Emiliano Martínez said he would be fit to return “in a few weeks” following surgery on a fractured jaw sustained during his team’s 2-0 Premier League win at Everton.

The Argentina international was taken to hospital after colliding with Everton defender Jarrad Branthwaite during the second half of Saturday’s game at Hill Dickinson Stadium. Martínez, 34, required eight minutes of treatment on the pitch before he was carried off on a stretcher. Chelsea boss Xabi Alonso later said he had suffered a concussion.

“Thanks to everyone for the messages. The operation went well,” Martínez wrote on social media on Sunday alongside a photo of himself in a hospital bed. “The most important thing is that we won, and kept a clean sheet. We’ll be back in a few weeks.”

Mike Penders is set to deputise in Martínez’s absence. The 21-year-old made his Premier League debut as a substitute against Everton. He joined from Belgian club Genk in August 2024 and has spent the past two seasons out on loan, including a spell at Strasbourg last term.

#75. Fabian Hurzeler breaks his Crystal Palace hoodoo as Brighton blow their bitter rivals away 5-0 to leave Pierre Sage smarting, writes NICK SZCZEPANIK

Published: 18:13 BST, 18 October 2026 | Updated: 18:39 BST, 18 October 2026

This match kicked off in a rainstorm of biblical proportions - and Brighton swept Crystal Palace away. This will take some getting over for the travelling fans, and their under-fire manager Pierre Sage.

Jaydee Canvot nodded Pascal Gross’s free kick into his own net after only four minutes and Diego Gomez hit a spectacular over the head of Walter Benitez from the half way line three minutes later, his first goal of the season. After nine minutes it was 3-0, Yasin Ayari’s shot deflecting in off the luckless Canvot.

Charalampos Kostoulas made it 4-0 early in the second half after Ayari’s shot from Gross’s cross had been blocked. Sussex-born sub Jack Hinshelwood – whose grandfather had played for Palace in the fixture – scored the fifth after Benitez had parried Luka Vuskovic’s header.

Brighton won the September goal of the month award thanks to a 25-yard thunderbolt from captain Lewis Dunk in their 5-0 win at Coventry.

And his teammate Gomez must surely be favourite for the October award. The ball was just crossing the half-way line when the Paraguay midfielder looked up and drove it fiercely goalwards, catching goalkeeper Benitez far enough off his line to have no chance of getting back.

This was no Beckhamesque lob, but a blast that succeeded through its power as much as its height and shock value, and it made him Brighton’s 11th different scorer in the league this season.

Diego Gomez scored a goal of the season contender from the halfway line as Brighton got off to a flying start

Many people unfamiliar with the history of this fixture question how two clubs some 45 miles apart can have a real rivalry. According to well-known motoring website, the distance between Selhurst Park and the Amex Stadium is about the same as that between Portman Road and Carrow Road, yet nobody questions the antagonism between Ipswich Town and Norwich City.

It all began in the mid-70s as the two clubs – managed by former Tottenham rivals Alan Mullery (Brighton) and Terry Venables (Palace) followed each other from the third division to the first and also clashed in a series of FA Cup ties.

The intense atmosphere has sometimes produced results that have defied league form, and home fans with memories of a few such games were concerned that Palace might burst the Brighton bubble despite the excellent recent performances that took them into the match in third place in the Premier League and as the division’s top scorers. Those fears were put to bed after just nine minutes.

Brighton head coach Fabian Hurzeler had yet to beat Palace in four meetings before Sunday.

On the eve of the game he said: 'In my journey so far with this club, we've experienced a lot of really, really positive things. But one thing is still missing.'

Not any more. He has built a team and a squad that exudes self-belief and they tore into Palace from the first whistle. Sage will hope he does not have to wait as long for his first win in the fixture.

Brighton exude self-belief and tore into their opponents from the first whistle to win 5-0

A section of the Brighton fans chanted “sacked in the morning” at Hurzeler during Palace’s 1-0 win at the Amex in February. But despite that nadir, owner Tony Bloom kept faith in the German, he pulled his team round and they qualified for the UEFA Conference League.

So this defeat may not do any long-lasting damage to the Eagles’ prospects in general and those of Sage in particular – despite gleeful “sacked in the morning” chants predictably directed at the Palace dugout. That said, Sage may have even greater cause today to feel grateful for last weekend's victory over Nottingham Forest and his predecessor, Oliver Glasner.

Both sides were in European action on Thursday, and Brighton’s squad strength told then as they were able to make eight changes and still stroll past FK Kauno Zalgiris 4-0, while Palace had a tougher evening in a 3-2 defeat away to Lyons.

Eight of Palace’s starting eleven here had also started that game while Brighton had seven fresh faces and it showed.

The Seagulls were again able to deploy the energetic high press that was too much for Arsenal in their previous home Premier League game. Brighton were first to every ball, even in the second half.

#76. Diego Gomez scores from halfway line as high-flying Brighton rout Crystal Palace

Please refresh the page or navigate to another page on the site to be automatically logged inPlease refresh your browser to be logged in

The Albion midfielder spectacularly opened his account for the season by pinging the ball over stranded Palace goalkeeper Walter Benitez

Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today.

Diego Gomez sensationally scored from the halfway line as Brighton struck three goals in the opening 10 minutes en route to thrashing bitter rivals Crystal Palace 5-0.

The Albion midfielder spectacularly opened his account for the season by pinging the ball over stranded Palace goalkeeper Walter Benitez from fractionally inside opposition territory.

His 51-metre finish conjured memories of David Beckham’s eye-catching effort against Wimbledon 30 years ago and was the longest-range Premier League goal since Wayne Rooney scored from 58 metres for Everton against West Ham in November 2017.

Jaydee Canvot’s own goal had set the Seagulls on course for a fourth successive top-flight win before Yasin Ayari’s deflected finish quickly added to Gomez’s stunner in a remarkable opening to the contest.

Charalampos Kostoulas added the fourth before Jack Hinshelwood completed the scoring after Eagles substitutes Jean-Philippe Mateta and Jefferson Lerma were denied consolations by the goal frame.

Brighton’s resounding victory was a first over Palace at the fifth attempt under head coach Fabian Hurzeler to move the high-flying south-coast club on to 16 points from seven games.

Eagles fans had packed the away end waving inflatable Conference League trophies to taunt Albion supporters but endured a humiliating afternoon in soggy Sussex as their outclassed side meekly surrendered.

Palace had won on their previous two visits to the Amex Stadium. Yet hope of repeating those results swiftly evaporated during a nightmare start for Pierre Sage’s side.

With less than four minutes gone, Seagulls midfielder Pascal Gross delivered an inswinging free-kick from the left and Eagles defender Canvot nodded into his own net from inside the six-yard box.

Away supporters, who began the match singing ‘Champions of Europe’ following their success in the Conference League last season, were again silenced just three minutes later by Gomez’s goal-of-the-season contender.

There appeared to be little danger when Palace captain Adam Wharton conceded possession just inside Brighton’s half.

However, following a pass from Olivier Boscagli, the alert Gomez spotted Benitez over his line and superbly found the net with a driven attempt.

Amid relentless rain, Palace boss Sage was left staring in disbelief on the touchline in the 10th minute when Ayari fired into the bottom-left corner via a deflection off Canvot after Albion forward Kostoulas back-heeled the ball back from the left.

The visitors continued to offer little in response, while Ferdi Kadioglu and Kostoulas threatened further punishment.

Brighton boss Hurzeler faced chants of “you’re getting sacked in the morning” during his team’s 1-0 home loss to the Eagles in February.

This was a significantly more enjoyable occasion, and scant hope of Palace fightback was extinguished four minutes into the second period when Kostoulas poked into the bottom-left corner after Ayari’s initial effort was blocked.

Mateta – making only his second appearance of the season following a hamstring injury – wasted a golden chance to pull one back by curling against the crossbar in the 63rd minute.

With many Eagles fans already heading back to south London, fellow replacement Lerma later nodded against the left post following a Wharton corner.

Palace’s misery was compounded six minutes from time when Hinshelwood poked home after Luka Vuskovic’s header was repelled by Benitez, leaving jubilant Brighton followers to celebrate a famous derby triumph.
