#816. Lisandro Martinez is one of the last to arrive at Man United training ahead of crunch talks with bosses after his explosive rant, while club renew pursuit of centre-back for January

Published: 11:57 BST, 15 October 2026 | Updated: 13:12 BST, 15 October 2026

Lisandro Martinez has returned to Man United's training ground for the first time since his explosive rant at the club's transfer policy.

Martinez gave a bombshell TV interview shortly after United's 2-0 defeat by Atletico Madrid, where he accused the Old Trafford board and director of football Jason Wilcox of failing in the transfer market last summer. Other senior players are understood to share his views.

United’s players had Wednesday off after flying straight back from Spain following the game, but reported for duty earlier today.

And Martinez was seen arriving at the club's Carrington base at around 9.50am in the back of a Toyota Ayoga. The Argentine was one of the last first-team players to turn up.

That was almost an hour after the under-fire Wilcox rocked up at 9am, and over two hours after Carrick's 7.25am arrival.

Daily Mail Sport reported on Wednesday that Martinez would face the music on Thursday in the wake of his blistering criticism of club bosses.

Lisandro Martinez (in the backseat of the car) was one of the last players to arrive at Man United training on Thursday morning

Michael Carrick arrived at 7:25am as his squad returned for the first time since Martinez's explosive rant at the club's hierarchy after their Champions League defeat by Atletico Madrid

Director of football Jason Wilcox, who was heavily criticised by Martinez, arrived at 9am

United were planning to decide what action – if any – to take against the Argentina international after spending Wednesday considering his outspoken comments and how they should respond, although it's understood that they are backing Wilcox.

It's believed Martinez's frustrations are a result of conversations with club executives over recent times and promises not being met.

Before last season, Martinez was told the club would rebuild and that he was fundamental to their plans, with the defender again informed at the end of the campaign that they were going to kick on.

Clubs in Spain were interested in Martinez in the summer but he wanted to stay and be part of Carrick's renaissance, yet his disappointment has developed after the aforementioned pledges weren't borne out in the calibre or quantity of recruitment.

Midfielders Youri Tielemans, Andrey Santos and Carlos Baleba and back-up goalkeeper Karl Darlow were the only summer additions, and Carrick's side look short in defence and in attack.

Martinez is a member of United's leadership group and there was a belief within the squad that they could challenge for titles with a bigger group, but many now feel they are undercooked in terms of depth.

One position where United have been keen to strengthen is at centre back, potentially even in January, but one must leave for that to happen.

Everton's Jarrad Branthwaite is admired, and while the club would rather not lose Martinez, his injury record and ability to attract a decent offer could make that option more acceptable following his comments.

United are also hoping to bring in a left-back after failing to do so in the summer when Lewis Hall signed a deal at Newcastle. Bournemouth and France star Adrien Truffert is a name on their radar.

Meanwhile, back in January, head coach Ruben Amorim was sacked after publicly criticising Wilcox but it’s highly improbable the club would take such a drastic approach with Martinez. A fine or warning reminding him of his responsibilities seems more likely.

Teammate Amad Diallo could also face questions on Thursday after he added more fuel to the fire with a message on social media after the Atletico game which read ‘f***ing disgrace, I have no words’, although it’s unclear what the Ivorian was referring to.

United are likely to need Martinez at Leeds with a number of injuries in defence. Luke Shaw, Patrick Dorgu and Noussair Mazraoui have been out of action, and Matthijs De Ligt only returned on the bench as an unused substitute in Madrid after nearly a year out with a back injury.

Martinez’s long-term future is more uncertain, however. He is out of contract at the end of June, although United can extend it by another year.

They are unlikely to let a 28-year-old World Cup winner leave as a free agent after his £57million move from Ajax in 2022, but could trigger the extension so they can demand a transfer fee for him.

Martinez took aim at the United hierarchy in the wake of a fourth defeat in nine games in Madrid when he was asked if the club have backed Michael Carrick enough. ‘I don't think so,’ he said. ‘He does his best. You can't keep changing, changing, changing the manager.

‘What about other areas? Tonight it is easy to say the coach and easy to say the players, but also we have to see other areas.

‘I expect more (investment) 100 per cent. I expect more from our technical director. I have to be honest, as players we have to do more but it is also important when you make a strong squad to be ready for this kind of night.

‘I have to control myself a lot but sometimes is a reflection of the mirror of how is our club at the moment.’

Martinez made the explosive comments in a TV interview shortly after the game ended in Spain

On Wednesday evening, Martinez then attempted to dilute his comments by explaining – but crucially not apologising – what he meant.

‘When I talk about wanting more, I’m talking about the ambition we must all have as part of this club,’ Martinez said, in part of his statement.

‘To keep growing, to become stronger and to have everything we need to compete at the highest level. These are standards we must all hold ourselves to, starting with me.’

He added: ‘We need to demand even more of ourselves and work together to take Manchester United back to the top. I believe in my team-mates, our manager and everyone working to help this club move forward.

‘I’m convinced that the way forward is to keep working together, with ambition and commitment. My goal has been the same since day one, to win, to compete at the highest level and to give everything I have for this badge.’

#817. Man City 2-4 PSG: This was some way for Enzo Maresca's side to lose - PSG continue to be the standard bearers, but City are not going to be shunted into irrelevance, writes IAN LADYMAN

Published: 22:16 BST, 14 October 2026 | Updated: 11:52 BST, 15 October 2026

Maybe nothing will be simple and straightforward for Manchester City ever again. Not the future, not the present. Not the politics and maybe not even the football.

Here against the Champions of Europe, with Pep Guardiola watching on from beneath his flat cap in the directors' box, Enzo Maresca's City threatened to follow the adrenaline shot of Sunday's win at Anfield with a complete flatline at the Etihad.

This for a while looked and felt like the night reality dawned. When all the noise and celebration and defiance of the weekend faded to grey. When the impact of playing the next weeks and months under the shadow of crushing uncertainty began to feel too much.

Three down to Luis Enrique's rampant PSG side after 31 minutes, City were on the verge of being embarrassed in front of their former coach and their own supporters. It was three and it could have been five. Goals for Desire Doue, Ousmane Dembele and Vitinha had ripped a hole in City's hearts.

Yet somehow, from the canvas, City found a pulse. They found a reaction, some adrenaline and – in the second-half – a comeback that did not quite serve as another two-fingered salute to the world but indicated at least that a coach and a group of players who have done absolutely nothing wrong are not going to be shunted into irrelevance as meekly as many would like.

City couldn't pull this off. To do so would have been quite ridiculous. But they terrified PSG in a second period played in an atmosphere of utter frenzy.

Vitinha (left) and Desire Doue (right) were both on the scoresheet for PSG in a rampant first half-hour

But Manchester City showed they will not fade into oblivion as they showed second-half fight

Erling Haaland scored twice for City in that spell and also hit the bar. Late on, with the score at 4-2, he almost slid one in at the far post. Heaven knows where that would have taken us all had it gone in.

A goal in between Haaland's brace from PSG's Maghnes Akliouche had ensured that City never quite got to within smelling distance. At the death, meanwhile, former City forward Ferran Torres, on as a substitute, missed a penalty for the French team.

At full-time, though, this huge modern stadium was still almost full. Maresca's team were applauded off after a lap of honour. How many teams get to do that having conceded four? These are strange and vaguely terrifying times for English football's most successful recent club but if and when City do tumble down the leagues, it appears they will do so together.

Even without the events of the last fortnight, this would have represented the biggest night of their season so far. After all their years of trying, PSG have finally established themselves as the standard bearers of European football.

For a while City merely flunked it. They were wretched without the ball during a first-half in which the game was ultimately lost. They were slow and lacking intelligence to the degree that the French team found far too much space in which to play.

As usual, PSG moved the ball devastatingly as they sought to exploit it. Even so, the way Doue was able to shoot low past two City defenders and in at Donnarumma's near post from 20 yards in the 13th minute was criminal from the point of view of the home team.

PSG's celebrations served as a tribute to the calibre of the opposition. This was a big night for Enrique's team too. Two minutes later they were dancing again.

This time the danger flowed down the right into space. Dembele's floated pass across goal to Doue was well judged and the way it was returned to him on the first-time half volley was sublime. As Dembele headed the ball down and in, it felt already like this game was over. It wasn't. Not quite.

Pep Guardiola watched on as his former side showed their credentials under Enzo Maresca

City tried to get a foothold. They hustled in midfield and tried to stretch PSG by using wingers Jeremy Doku and Antoine Semenyo whenever possible. All the while, though, PSG carried that latent threat.

The speed at which they carried the ball upfield was as alarming as it was thrilling. Just after the half hour, right-back Achraf Hakimi headed a Doue cross back across goal and against the post but it didn't matter. From the next phase of play his team scored anyway.

Donnarumma's clearance came back towards City on halfway and every PSG player who touched the ball in the ensuing passage did so at their own apparent leisure. Only when it was moved to the edge of the City penalty area did the pace quicken.

Warren Zaire-Emery's back heel flick to Vitinha was perfect and the Portuguese international drilled the ball in from 16 yards.

City's choice options were now clear. Shrivel and die or find something from within. It was to their credit that they took the latter. Twice before half-time they threatened, through Doku and Haaland. Then, in a frantic and quite extraordinary second-half, they persistently threatened to claw their way back.

Three times in five early minutes, City could have scored. A Semenyo shot was deflected over, Enzo Fernandez headed wide and then substitute Iliman Ndiaye was denied point blank by Matvei Safonov at his near post.

With the crowd energised, City rode a wave of fresh adrenaline. In the 53rd minute, Ndiaye crossed and Haaland scored with a flick header. Briefly something truly extraordinary was on. It was PSG's turn to look a little lost.

After further flurries of City attacking activity, Akliouche turned well to shoot high from 18 yards and Donnarumma could only watch as the ball flew up off his outstretched hand and landed back down over the goal line. Once again the outcome felt settled. Once again City came back.

Josko Gvardiol had a header cleared off the line by Nuno Mendes as the hosts battled

City showed despite the loss that if and when they fall down the leagues they will do so together

Josko Gvardiol saw a header cleared from the line before Haaland landed one on the bar. And then, with 15 minutes still remaining, Haaland side footed in his team's second goal from inside the area.

City kept surging forwards. This was gripping, crazy playground football and chances came on the back of it. Maresca's team ended the night having taken 27 of the night's 42 shots. It was some way to lose.

Manchester City: (4-2-3-1) Donnarumma 5; Khusanov 5, Ruben Dias 5 (Matheus Nunes 46 5), Guehi 6. Gvardiol 5; Anderson 6, Fernandez 6 (O'Reilly 90); Semenyo 6, Cherki 5 (Ndiaye 46mins 7), Doku 6 (Bouaddi 46 7); Haaland 6

Subs not used: Rulli, Bettinelli, Reis, Lewis, Ait-Nouri, Foden, Kovacic, Allan

PSG: (4-3-3) Safonov 6; Hakimi 6, Marquinhos 6, Pacho 7, Nuno Mendes 6; Zaire-Emery 7 (Beraldo 84), Vitinha 7, Fabian Ruiz 6 (Hernandez 84); Akliouche 7 (Neves 76 6), Dembele 7 (Torres 76 4), Doue 8 (Kvaratskhelia 66 6)

Subs not used: Chevalier, Mouak, Zabarnyi, Digne, Fernandez, Godts, Ndjantou

Goals: Doue 13, Dembele 15, Vitinha 32, Akliouche 63

#819. Harry Maguire and Bruno Fernandes would be 'too busy doing podcasts' to pull up Lisandro Martinez for Man United rant, taunts Roy Keane - as Steven Bartlett is caught in crossfire

Published: 10:05 BST, 15 October 2026 | Updated: 11:43 BST, 15 October 2026

Roy Keane has accused Manchester United's dressing room leaders of being too busy podcasting to enforce dressing room discipline.

The Red Devils legend thinks Harry Maguire and Bruno Fernandes don't have the nerve to chastise Lisandro Martinez after his explosive outburst about the club.

Martinez criticised the club's bosses and claimed they should have signed more players over the summer after their 2-0 defeat at Atletico Madrid on Tuesday night.

For Keane it is symptomatic of a club culture where players air their grievances instead of working hard to improve – a mentality set by the senior players.

'Bruno, Maguire... they're probably busy doing podcasts, I can't imagine them pulling him (Martinez). Bruno's body language, he doesn't seem a happy lad at the moment. They're pulling nobody,' he told the Stick to Football podcast.

'This reflects where Manchester United are and where this dressing room is. Maguire gets left out of the England squad - he's all upset with that. Instead of rolling his sleeves up during the summer, "I'm going to go to New York and do a podcast for a few weeks". That's his mindset.

Roy Keane has claimed Bruno Fernandes and Harry Maguire are 'too busy doing podcasts' to discipline Lisandro Martinez (YouTube: The Overlap)

The duo both went on podcasts over the summer to talk about their grievances

Martinez hit out at the club's hierarchy and hinted the squad was too weak in an explosive rant

'I made a mistake with Bruno (Fernandes) on this programme. Bruno goes on a podcast with (Steven Bartlett), this is the Man United captain, he goes on there, has a little dig at me, no problem, he's entitled to respond.

'That's the mindset of a Man United player, I'm going to start doing these little gigs instead of getting Man United competing at the very top.

'So this idea, when I see a player have a little b**** the last few days, I'd be more annoyed at Maguire and Bruno for getting things off their chests on podcasts. You get your priorities in place as a footballer.

'Back in our day it was more magazines than podcasts, but if a player went off and said something, even silly, he'd come in the dressing room, and lads would say: "What are you talking about?" You'd put him in his place in that sense - not a big bust-up.

'Man United is a circus. If you can, try and do your talking on the pitch. If you have to let off a bit of steam, ok, but try and do it on the back of some victories, or when you've won a league title or something like that.

'These players have done nothing for the last few years at Man United. Two years ago we were finishing 13th (15th) or whatever, getting knocked out by Grimsby, and they're coming up with all these comments.'

The panel of Keane, Gary Neville, Steven Gerrard, Ian Wright, and Jill Scott agreed that Martinez calling for more signings could upset members of the dressing room.

The Argentinian had said on Tuesday: 'I expect more (investment) 100 per cent. I expect more from our technical director. I have to be honest, as players we have to do more but it is also important when you make a strong squad to be ready for this kind of night.

Diary of a CEO host Steven Bartlett was caught in the crossfire of Keane's comments

'We did a fantastic season last season and now we expect more from the top, more players to compete because many teams bring many players as well.'

And Neville hit back: 'What he says is right, they should have brought in more defenders. However, you can't say that as a player.

'If you say that publicly as a player, you're effectively saying that the players I'm playing with are not good enough. That's where the players have to pick him up.

'If you're Leny Yoro or Ayden Heaven, and you've got a little doubt about settling into the first-team, and you're a young player, you're thinking: "My World Cup-winning centre-back has said we should have brought more players in so I don't play", you're really feeling nervous and anxious.'

Keane argued it was a matter of semantics: 'I'm sure we said it back in the day. Big clubs, new players help you improve. You'd say it in certain ways - "we need competition for places".

'"We had a fantastic season last year" - there you go. That's where he's coming from. He actually thinks they had a fantastic season. Fine him two weeks' wages for saying that!'

Martinez has not covered himself in glory as of late, scoring a comical own goal against Fulham and arguably being at fault for Dominic Solanke's goal in the 1-1 draw with Tottenham last weekend.

Daily Mail Sport's Nathan Salt handed him a rating of five for his performance against Atletico, writing that it was an improvement on his Spurs showing but still with 'hairy moments'.

He added: ‘We need to demand even more of ourselves and work together to take Manchester United back to the top. I believe in my team-mates, our manager and everyone working to help this club move forward.

The impact of Martinez’s initial statement is still likely to be felt through until Sunday’s trip to face Leeds United at Elland Road, while team-mate Amad Diallo is also in the spotlight after he added more fuel to the fire with a message on social media which read ‘f***ing disgrace, I have no words’, although it’s unclear what the Ivorian was referring to.

#820. Pep Guardiola tried to be incognito but the ex-Man City manager's presence was felt on his return with demands his big moments are expunged entirely from history, writes JACK GAUGHAN

Published: 07:00 BST, 15 October 2026 | Updated: 11:42 BST, 15 October 2026

A returning hero at the Etihad, invited back for the night. Ali Benarbia, the mercurial midfielder, is considered a legend of a former Manchester City era as they won the First Division title in the early Noughties. He knows the second tier well etcetera, etcetera.

But then there was the other guy. The other guy didn’t do club media and interviews on the pitch but his presence fills an arena regardless.

Flat caps became a thing for Pep Guardiola when Mike Summerbee took him to tailors Williams & Gill on Chapel Street after taking over. He bought one for £75 and has in the past worn them as a tribute to the late life president Bernard Halford.

It was, at one stage, a symbol of Guardiola and Manchester. Less of a symbol when heading inside the place he called home for a decade on Wednesday. Instead, apparel to slightly conceal the identity of somebody who wanted to keep this return as low key as possible.

He emerged from the Chairman’s Lounge in the Colin Bell Stand nine minutes before kick off, taking a seat on the third row of the directors’ box behind Ferran Soriano and Khaldoon Al Mubarak, just as the club started playing a montage of great moments – Yaya Toure at Wembley, the Dennis Tueart bicycle kick, Bernardo Silva and Real Madrid – that stirred a fanbase visiting here for the first time since their world fell in.

Guardiola was sat alongside confidante Manel Estiarte in the seats he had spun on his heels and pointed towards hundreds of times when celebrating goals during a period of dominance that City’s fiercest critics want expunged entirely from history.

Pep Guardiola might have wanted to hide under his flat cap upon returning to the Etihad but his presence - a show of support - shouted loudly

Seated a few rows behind the current Man City hierarchy Guardiola was frequently locked in conversation with his old coaching assistant Manel Estiarte

He winced and he scratched the beard as Paris Saint-Germain ripped through the team he loves so dearly in a first half of glitteringly rapid dominance, with quickfire goals bearing some hallmarks of a few painful European nights on the Catalan’s watch.

This is a City side in its infancy and will need more nights against the very best in Europe, which PSG obviously are, before they look more comfortable in their new skin. Yet as it stands, those opportunities are likely to end once this season is over. A team destined for League Two cannot possibly compete with the vast riches of the Champions League kings.

The hierarchy, including chairman Al Mubarak, will have felt it important that Guardiola made the journey. As a show of support behind the club’s insistence of innocence heading into their appeal.

The 55-year-old had been in Abu Dhabi, where he is having a property built, last week and arrived in Manchester hours before this tie. He entered the main stand at a time when the congregated thousands were not waiting for the arrival of the coach carrying Enzo Maresca’s squad and clearly did not want to detract from those players or provide a distraction for his successor.

City didn’t make a song and dance about his attendance and that is how he’d rather it. Guardiola flashed up on the big screen once as some supporters inside this place must have been wrestling with how to feel and react to what has been a deluge dumped upon them over the past fortnight.

The volume dialled up once City found a foothold and started bossing the ball with more certainty, albeit three down by that point. It proves that watching this team play well, irrespective of what it ultimately may mean over the coming months, can provide some escapism for people who are suddenly having to morph into legal and financial experts – with an outside expectance for them to act as moral arbiters – around something that is supposed to be a hobby.

That will not stop until this whole thing ends. And even then it might not. Yet as City fought back, attacking with heart and gumption, there will remain performances to cherish for however long the fans’ purgatory lasts.

He watched Coventry lose to Hull in August wearing a blue-strapped watch worth £102,000

'I walk the dog a lot and I find it is good for clearing the head and for that, I like going to the gym as well. That is another one of my superstitions. I have to do exactly the same amount of time on the bike, 50 minutes, or the exact same route that I run.

‘If I don’t do the routines I feel, ridiculously, like it might have an effect on results. But sometimes I do miss the dog walk for some reason.’

With a trip to winless Tottenham up next, Lampard may be reluctant to part with his new lucky timepiece as Coventry head to north London on Monday.

#826. Martin O'Neill urges Celtic to channel the spirit of 1967 and stun Benfica in Lisbon

By CALUM CROWE, SCOTTISH DEPUTY CHIEF SPORTS WRITER

Published: 22:30 BST, 14 October 2026 | Updated: 23:25 BST, 14 October 2026

Celtic boss Martin O’Neill has challenged his players to channel the spirit of the Lisbon Lions and produce a Europa League shock against Benfica.

Thousands of Celtic supporters have descended on Lisbon over the past couple of days, with this season marking the 60th anniversary of the club’s finest hour when they beat Inter Milan to lift the European Cup.

Celtic will start as huge underdogs at the Estadio da Luz against a slick Benfica side who are among the favourites to go all the way and win the competition.

The Portuguese side got their Europa League campaign up and running with a terrific 2-0 win away against AC Milan in the San Siro last month.

Celtic, meanwhile, are already behind the eight-ball after losing their opening match 3-1 against Ferencvaros in Glasgow a few weeks ago.

But O’Neill is hopeful that the sense of history in Lisbon can inspire his players to what would be a seismic result.

Celtic boss Martin O'Neill addresses the media in Lisbon ahead of the clash with Benfica

Celtic skipper Callum McGregor trudges off as Celtic lost on matchday one to Ferencvaros

‘First of all, we’re looking forward to the game, it’s a big match for us,’ said O’Neill, who hopes to have Camilo Duran involved following the birth of his child.

‘You’re right about the history of the football club and its connection to Lisbon, so it’s terrific. It’s something I think the football club should be really proud of.

‘I think a lot of the players have seen the stadium (Estadio Nacional, venue for the 1967 European Cup Final) from before (during a pre-season trip two years ago), so I guess they’re aware of the history.

‘It’s really lovely, something to look forward to. I think that just the whole history of it should have a galvanising effect for us.

‘Listen, we are under no illusions, we know it will be difficult. Benfica are a fine side. They will be disappointed not to be in the Champions League and will be among the favourites to win this competition.

‘The point I want to make is that while the European games are hard, they are exciting at the same time.

‘It’s lovely, even now, for me to come here to Lisbon and try and win a game against Benfica. We want to have a real go.’

Asked for his own personal memories of watching Celtic’s victory over Inter Milan in 1967, O’Neill continued: ‘I can remember watching the game. Of course I do, absolutely.

‘I was at a boarding school at the time. There were around 200 boarders, stretching from 11 years of age up to 18.

‘I was around 15 at the time and we were allowed to watch the game. It was a black and white TV and we all gathered around it - and before the game started it stopped working.

‘Then one of the priests came down, gave it a thump on the back, and it started to work again. We thought he’d worked a miracle!

Celtic will be without defender Cameron Carter-Vickers for the Europa League game at Benfica

‘So we saw the whole game and Celtic were brilliant. I’ve never been to the stadium but I’d love to go. I intend to do it.

‘There may even be a possibility of going before our game. We’ll see how the day goes.’

Despite the fact that Celtic lost their opening match to Ferencvaros, O’Neill remains adamant that the European campaign should not be viewed as a write-off.

Celtic dropped down into the Europa League on the back of the collapse against LASK Linz in the Champions League qualifiers after blowing a four-goal lead.

Confident they can yet go on a run and achieve something this season, the 74-year-old continued: ‘First of all, we’re going to try and qualify for the knockout stages for a start.

‘We did that last year and that’s what we’re trying to do. We’ve got another seven games in which to try and get enough points to qualify.

‘I don’t know what would do it. Ten or eleven or something against you would qualify. So that would be the ambition for us to do it.’

Celtic will be without Cameron Carter-Vickers as he continues to recover from a hamstring strain.

But O’Neill is hopeful that Duran will be able to fly out and join the team in time for tonight’s match following the birth of his baby.

Duran has been Celtic’s best player this season. The Colombian forward was on the scoresheet in the 2-0 win over Motherwell last weekend and has netted seven goals so far this term.

‘He should come out and join us,’ added O’Neill. ‘It’ll be great to have him with us. His partner has had the baby, so it’s brilliant.

‘There is a possibility of trying to get something organised to fly him out to Lisbon this evening. But failing that he’ll travel tomorrow (Thursday).’

Celtic goalkeeper Viljami Sinisalo speaks to the press in Portugal

Meanwhile, Celtic goalkeeper Viljami Sinisalo admits it came as a shock to lose his place to Sam Johnstone a few weeks ago.

Sinisalo was dropped for two games last month, one of which was the 3-0 defeat to Rangers at Ibrox in the Premier Sports Cup.

Former England international Johnstone, who arrived at Celtic on a season-long loan from Wolves, struggled to convince before O’Neill swiftly reverted back to Sinisalo.

Now established as first-choice once again, Sinisalo is determined to hold on to the gloves now and showcase his best form.

Asked whether it had been a surprise to be dropped, the Finland international said: ‘I suppose it was, yeah. I’ll put it bluntly, yeah, it was a surprise, but that’s ultimately a decision that was made.

‘That’s gone now, you can’t really focus on it too much. It’s gone and now it’s down to me in terms of staying in the team.

‘Like I said, I need to perform in a manner that there isn’t a conversation. I don’t want there to be a conversation (about who is No 1), that’s the bottom line.

‘I don’t want that to happen again. It’s quite simple. I’ve waited a long time, worked hard and played a lot of games now.

‘Over the last 30 games roughly, I think I played 28 or something like that. Once you get a bit of taste of that, you don’t want to let it go.

‘It’s what you want to do. It gives you that little fire in the belly to say: “This is my time now”. It’s up to me to keep playing well and keep the position.’

That makes it 78 goals in 18 games in the second game of the Champions League group phase, and frankly, that is just daft. There's entertainment, and then there is that.

The chosen one saw his Porto side pick up just one point from his opening two games while Inter’s victorious 2009/10 campaign kicked off with two draws in the group stage.

The only other manager to achieve this feat? A certain Scotsman in 1999… that's right, Sir Alex Ferguson with Manchester United.

#830. Unai Emery's 'no excuses' culture finally pays off and how Nicolas Jackson proved he was signed for more than just goals, writes TOM COLLOMOSSE - as Villans hit Fenerbahce for SIX

Published: 22:02 BST, 14 October 2026 | Updated: 22:26 BST, 14 October 2026

No North Stand, no problem. Aston Villa delivered their most emphatic European win and their first home victory of the campaign as Mason Greenwood made an anonymous return to an English stadium.

The former Manchester United winger, who last played in England in January 2022, was barracked throughout by the home fans.

Greenwood was dropped from the United first team when he was arrested and charged with attempted rape, assault and controlling and coercive behaviour in October 2022, before charges and the case were dropped in February 2023 when key witnesses withdrew. He has denied any wrongdoing.

The 25-year-old was one of Fenerbahce’s highest-profile signings last summer but struggled in the duel with former United team-mate Aaron Wan-Bissaka.

By contrast, Villa excelled against the desperately poor Turkish giants, with Johan Manzambi and a double from Nicolas Jackson making the game safe before half-time. Ross Barkley added two more – one from the spot – in the second half and substitute Tammy Abraham made it a record win.

Daily Mail Sport looks at the main talking points from Villa’s second straight Champions League win, achieved with the Prince of Wales watching from the directors’ box.

Aston Villa made history with their most emphatic win in Europe against Fenerbahce

Tammy Abraham was the last of the goal scorers with Ross Barkley and Johan Manzambi among the scorers

Villa's most famous fan Prince William was in high spirits as he took in the night at Villa Park

Villa boss Unai Emery will never allow his side to blame poor results on external factors. That means he rejects the idea that Villa will suffer by playing in a three-sided ground.

The club hope to take their capacity beyond 50,000 in time for the start of next season but in the meantime, one end of the ground is a building site. Villa need a bigger ground to make more money and that means shutting one end of it for a minimum one season.

Before this clash Villa had lost to Arsenal and Nottingham Forest and drawn with Brentford here but Emery would not allow players or fans to dwell on their quieter ground.

‘Not ideal, but never an excuse,’ said Emery. ‘We must accept the sacrifice of being without the North Stand, but we also understand it is for the greater good.

‘Because next season, and for years to come, Villa Park will be a stadium with greater capacity, improved facilities and an even more extraordinary atmosphere.

‘It is like when we have an injured important player. We must accept, not cry, and everyone has to deliver their best to overcome this situation.’

As weak as Fener were, Villa were sharper than they have been all season here. Johan Manzambi is growing with every match and deserved his goal, which took a huge deflection off Milan Skriniar. Wan-Bissaka looked comfortable and Boubacar Kamara looked much more like himself.

Nobody said it would be easy playing in front of fewer fans and there were less than 35,000 at this one. Just don’t let Emery hear you moaning about it.

Unai Emery has not wanted to place the blame for Villa's sluggish start on anything other than what he can control

Nicolas Jackson offers Emery more than just goals - although he bagged a 10-minute brace on the night

We have questioned many of Villa’s transfers in these pages so it is only fair we applaud them when they get one right.

Many online were quick to mock Emery when he paid £65million for a player who had struggled towards the end of his career at Chelsea, when he seemed to collect more yellow cards than goals.

But Emery had worked with Jackson at Villarreal and knew exactly what he could offer. The Senegal forward now has five goals in all competitions – bear in mind Ollie Watkins, the man he replaced, did not reach that tally last season until December 27.

Jackson is about more than the goals. His pace stretches defences but his link play is solid too, meaning he is developing a nice understanding with Manzambi.

His goals were similar – clean right-footed efforts from just outside the box that found the bottom corner, though former Manchester City pair Ederson and Nathan Ake should have done much better with Jackson’s second.

Jackson was probably aggrieved to be denied the chance of a hat-trick when Barkley took the ball for the penalty but he could be very happy with his night’s work.

Mason Greenwood's return to English soil was a disappointment in a dire Fenerbahce side

If Ederson and Ake had played like this when they were at City, they would not have won so many trophies.

The Brazil goalkeeper was so sluggish in trying to save Jackson’s strike and Ake was even worse. He made little attempt to block Jackson’s shot and like the rest of his team, looked barely interested for most of the game.

Fener have signed too many players whose best days are behind them. Happily for Villa fans, their team have gone the opposite way. In Manzambi, Ibrahim Mbaye and Jackson, Villa have serious pace, skill and unpredictability in attack and they can trouble many teams in this European campaign.

Aston Villa (4-2-3-1): Suzuki 7; Cash 6, Lindelof 7, Torres 8, Wan-Bissaka 7; Kamara 7 (Alysson 73), Barkley 8 (Goretzka 83); Mbaye 7 (Garnacho 78), McGinn 7, Manzambi 8 (Gomes 73); *JACKSON 9* (Abraham 78)

Scorers: Manzambi 12, Jackson 31, 39, Barkley 68 (pen), 72

Fenerbahce (4-2-3-1): Ederson 5; Semedo 5, Skriniar 4, Ake 4, Brown 6; Guendouzi 5, Yuksek 5 (Elmaz 69, 6); Greenwood 5 (Lukaku 69, 6), Kahveci 5, Aydin 7; Muriqi 6 (Nene 69, 6).

#831. Man City fans send defiant unity message with a giant tifo of support at the Etihad in their first home match since guilty verdict

Published: 20:11 BST, 14 October 2026 | Updated: 21:19 BST, 14 October 2026

Manchester City fans again threw their support behind their team in their first home game since they were found guilty of the vast majority of their financial charges against the Premier League.

The club's fans displayed a giant tifo reading 'CTID' before kick-off in the Champions League against Paris Saint-Germain – which stands for 'City 'til I die'.

City are appealing their verdict, which could see them face significant punishment if the decision is upheld.

They played their first game since the verdict against Liverpool on Sunday, winning 3-0.

Their fans opted to see the sunny side of things in mocking their situation, with Liverpool supporters chanting that the club are 'cheats'.

City fans, though, like their players, continue to support their club.

Manchester City fans threw their support behind their club with a giant tifo before their Champions League game against PSG

They continue to back the club and chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak in the battle with the Premier League

Another sign on show read: 'In Khaldoon we trust - we've won it all!'

Erling Haaland said after the game against Liverpool: 'Every single person part of Man City, and every fan, this is a lovely moment that will stay with us for a long time.

'It was tough, it was hard but we showed amazing character from back to front. So proud of everyone. (It's) important to stay strong mentally, stick together and do what you can do something about, and the thing we can do something about is to play good football and fight together. That's the only thing we can do.'

Former City manager Pep Guardiola, meanwhile, was sat in Manchester City's directors' box for the tie, seated behind chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak and chief executive Ferran Soriano.

The Spaniard, who won six Premier League titles during his ten-year stint in Manchester, also threw his support behind his former side.

The 55-year-old has been replaced by Enzo Maresca, with the new boss now having to contend with the explosive fallout of the Premier League bombshell verdict, in which City have been found guilty of the vast majority of the 115 charges against them.

The era covering the charges – from 2009 to 2018 – laid the foundations for Guardiola's huge success at the Etihad Stadium, and has called into question the legendary manager's legacy as a result.

City have strenuously denied any wrongdoing and have launched an appeal against the verdict, while Guardiola took to Instagram in the wake of the findings to publicly back his former club.

#832. Back at the same venue of the famous Lisbon Lions European Cup triumph almost 60 years ago, Celtic are trying to fight their way back to relevance on the big stage

By CALUM CROWE, SCOTTISH DEPUTY CHIEF SPORTS WRITER

Published: 19:01 BST, 14 October 2026 | Updated: 21:10 BST, 14 October 2026

Over the past 24 hours or so, thousands of Celtic fans have descended on Lisbon.

A city to which their club will forever be linked in the most romantic terms, making the journey here is a rite of passage.

Especially with this season marking the 60th anniversary of the Lisbon Lions, it is a pilgrimage to a place of spiritual and emotional significance, one which is woven into the fabric of the club.

Bathed in the most glorious sunshine, the old Estadio Nacional felt like it had come alive yesterday afternoon.

The trees and shrubbery which surround the stadium eventually cast long shadows over the pitch. Up on the steps, the silhouette of Billy McNeill lifting the European Cup would have been visible to many.

One of the tour guides, Carlos, was doing his best to bridge the language barrier between Portuguese and Glaswegian.

Celtic captain Billy McNeill with the European Cup in 1967

Celtic celebrate Stevie Chalmers' goal in the 1967 European Cup win over Inter Milan in Lisbon

For the many thousands of Celtic fans who have made this journey over the years, they are united by the memory and wider resonance of that victory over Inter Milan.

The 59 years which have passed have only burnished its romance. An exhibition titled ‘From Glasgow to Glory,’ occupies the tunnel of the Estadio Nacional itself.

The hours have been extended this week so that the travelling support can walk the same path that Jock Stein and his players once took.

They will stand where McNeill stood and they will feel the weight of what was achieved. For many, it is a necessary communion with the club’s finest hour.

Yet, truthfully, the Celtic team that have arrived here under Martin O’Neill for a Europa League clash with Benfica tonight is a million miles removed from those former glories. The contrast is almost cruel.

Earlier this week, there was a line from Celtic defender Liam Scales which referenced the Europa League victory away to Feyenoord last season as an example of winning against the odds.

Turning back the clock to that night in Rotterdam last November, where Celtic would claim a 3-1 victory, the words of O’Neill are worth revisiting.

Speaking pre-match, as he prepared to hand over the reins to Wilfried Nancy a few days later, O’Neill was asked to give his thoughts on what it might take for Celtic to get back competing at the top level again.

‘Jock Stein said it - European football is where Celtic should be,’ said O’Neill in his media conference deep in the bowels of De Kuip.

‘But at this minute it’s a struggle for us. Recruitment is important. In the next couple of years, Celtic will come again in European football.’

The chance to lead a revival in Europe and for Celtic to ‘come again’, in O’Neill’s words, were unquestionably a major factor in his decision to stay and have another crack at it this season.

The Celtic team are pictured with the European Cup in 1967

Celtic return to a hero's welcome at Parkhead after becoming the first British team to win the European Cup

However, right now, the painful reality is that Celtic look further away than ever before in terms of being able to make a tangible impact in European competition.

Only Stein stands above O’Neill in the pantheon of Celtic’s all-time greatest managers. Yet, for all the residual affection that is attached to his name, his team have lost their way.

The scar tissue from that Champions League collapse against LASK Linz, where Celtic blew a four-goal lead, still runs deep.

A torrid week in September left Celtic with three consecutive defeats: twice to Rangers and once, embarrassingly, 3-1 at home to Ferencvaros in the opening match of this Europa League league phase.

O’Neill spoke afterwards of reflection and of the possibility that it might be time to ‘wrap it up’. The international break allowed cooler and calmer counsel to prevail.

He has chosen to stay. The club, for its part, has offered public support. Yet the doubts that surround the side have not evaporated on the basis of a 2-0 victory over Motherwell last weekend.

With Cameron Carter-Vickers once again absent through injury, Celtic could line up with a back four tonight of Colby Donovan, Liam Scales, Dane Murray and Kieran Tierney.

The fact that they spent good money at the top end of the pitch in the summer is irrelevant in the respect that any team is only as strong as their weakest links.

Going up against a team of Benfica’s quality with the likes of Murray and Scales at centre-back is why so many Celtic fans who hadn’t travelled to Lisbon will watch this match through the cracks of their fingers from behind the sofa.

Digging through some of the numbers, few would blame them. Celtic have kept just two clean sheets in their last 29 Europa League matches.

Celtic walk out in the Portuguese son for their mdate with destiny almost 60 years ago

Benfica at the Estadio da Luz are a formidable prospect. Just last season, whilst under the command of Jose Mourinho, they beat Real Madrid 4-2 in the Champions League here in Lisbon.

Mourinho left to take charge of Madrid for a second time in the summer and has since been replaced by his Portuguese compatriot Marco Silva.

During his time in the English Premier League with the likes of Fulham, Everton, Watford and Hull City, it often felt like Silva divided opinion.

But he has made a good start with Benfica. Silva’s side have won nine of their last ten matches across all competitions. Their only loss in their last 14 matches came recently against Porto.

A couple of months ago, Wouter Vrancken’s Hearts were battered 6-1 in a Europa League qualifier here in Lisbon.

Vangelis Pavlidis was among the goalscorers that night and the Greek striker has been in electric form with 14 goals in 14 matches so far this season.

Celtic fans probably hoped to see a similar sort of return from Kasper Hogh after he joined for a club record fee of £11million in the summer.

But Hogh has struggled to justify that price tag. He looks to be a striker short on confidence and lacking the capabilities to lead the line for Celtic.

If O’Neill can start to get more of a tune out of Hogh, especially in these big games, it would go a long way to turning things around. A resurgent Hearts at Parkhead on Sunday will be another major test.

Celtic manager Jock Stein lifts the European Cup

O’Neill’s predicament is not merely one of results. There is a growing sense of toxicity between the club’s support and its ownership.

Protests directed at principal shareholder Dermot Desmond have brought the whole thing to the surface again. Desmond’s subsequent response in a club statement had the effect of pouring petrol on the flames.

O’Neill has spoken of the rift as ‘really sad’ and insisted that such matters lie beyond his control. He is right, of course.

A manager can only deal with the players in front of him and the matches they face. Yet the broader context of discontent cannot be ignored.

The more that O’Neill chooses to align himself with Desmond by claiming that these protests ‘are not Celtic’, the more he risks alienating himself from the fanbase and tarnishing his legacy.

In a way, he can’t win. In a city which once offered the purest reflection of Celtic’s identity as a club, what now stares back at them is a pale imitation.

The Lisbon Lions did not merely win a European Cup in this city. They created a legacy that continues to define what this club aspires to be.

The present side are a million miles removed from living up to it. What happens against Benfica tonight could well highlight that chasm with painful clarity.

At the Estadio da Luz, or the Stadium of Light in English, it is O’Neill and Celtic who are still trying to fight their way through the darkness of European irrelevance.

#833. FIFA insiders allege Gianni Infantino told Donald Trump he'd 'take care of' USA star's World Cup red card during murky phone call

By DANIEL MATTHEWS, US SENIOR SPORTS WRITER

Published: 19:09 BST, 14 October 2026 | Updated: 21:06 BST, 14 October 2026

FIFA president Gianni Infantino personally intervened to suspend Folarin Balogun's World Cup red card following a call with President Trump, a bombshell new report has claimed.

In a saga that sparked condemnation from across the world, the striker was originally barred from the USA's last-16 match against Belgium, only for his ban to be sensationally suspended by the FIFA disciplinary committee following a protest by the White House. Now the New York Post claims that Infantino told Trump in a call on July 1 that 'he would take care of it. One call and it was done.'

FIFA did not comment on the new claims but pointed to a July statement from Infantino, when he insisted the decision was made by ‘independent’ bodies acting ‘autonomously.’

The claims are nevertheless likely to pile more pressure on the FIFA president, who is in Switzerland this week for a council meeting that some expect to be 'explosive'. His position is already under threat after a number of controversies over the past year. Back in December, Infantino awarded Trump the inaugural FIFA Peace Prize – to widespread ridicule.

During the World Cup, the Balogun affair saw Infantino accused of favoritism and caving to the White House, while the FIFA president and Trump were mocked for handing over the trophy to Spain together.

Before long, Infantino faced a mutiny over his secret plans – later scrapped – to sell a stake in the World Cup to private equity investors including Joshua Kushner, the brother of Trump's son-in-law Jared Kushner.

Gianni Infantino reportedly intervened to suspend Folarin Balogun's World Cup red card

The striker was sent off for a tackle during their 2-0 win over Bosnia and Herzegovina

Back in July, Balogun was sent off during the USA's win over Bosnia and Herzegovina, with FIFA regulations stipulating that red cards can only be appealed in the case of mistaken identity, or if a player was facing a multi-game suspension.

But Trump later confirmed that he had asked Infantino to 'review' the sending off.

'All I did was ask for a review. I didn't say, you have to do this,' the President said. 'This man is a smart, tough man, Gianni Infantino.

'He's a smart, tough man, and his stock has gone through the roof because the job he has done has been great. I feel like we have to have all the best players on the field.'

Though Balogun was cleared to play, the USMNT suffered a 4-1 loss to Belgium which cut short their World Cup campaign.

US-born Canada coach Jesse Marsch later said: 'What I feel when the Balogun ruling happens is that would never happen in any other country in the world, and this is why everyone around the world hates America.'

Amid the backlash, Infantino released a statement which read: 'I have seen the public comments regarding the decision of the independent FIFA Disciplinary Committee related to the suspension of Folarin Balogun, and I would like to reiterate a fundamental principle of FIFA’s governance.

'FIFA’s judicial bodies are independent. They operate autonomously, apply the FIFA Disciplinary Code, and decide cases based on the applicable regulations and the specific facts before them.

'Their independence is essential to the credibility and integrity of football, and this must always be respected.

Trump later confirmed that he had asked FIFA president Infantino to 'review' the sending off

The USMNT crashed out of the World Cup following a 4-1 loss to Belgium in Seattle

'Yes, I regularly discuss matters related to the FIFA World Cup with the President of the United States, and on this matter, I did receive a call from President Donald Trump, just as I receive calls from heads of state, government officials, football stakeholders and business executives from around the world on many different issues.

'During our conversation, I explained that there was an ongoing legal process involving FIFA’s independent judicial bodies and that the case would be decided in due course by the competent bodies.

'That is how FIFA’s system works, and it is a principle that I will always uphold. I read the decisions of the FIFA Disciplinary Committee when they are issued. Sometimes I am surprised by them. Sometimes I agree with them, and sometimes I disagree.

'What I always do, however, is respect those decisions and the autonomy of the bodies that make them. Whether we personally like a decision or not is irrelevant. Respect for independent institutions and the rule of law is what protects the integrity of our competitions and the credibility of FIFA at all times.'

The Post also reports that, on the eve of a FIFA council meeting this week, soccer chiefs proposed a disciplinary code change that 'forbids FIFA legal panels from suspending automatic one-game bans for red cards'.

A source insisted the move would only put the change up for discussion at the upcoming FIFA meeting and was neither an emergency attempt to rewrite the rules nor an admission of guilt over the Balogun affair.

Earlier this month, meanwhile, former Tottenham defender Ramon Vega announced his intention to challenge Infantino at next year's FIFA presidential election.

Despite mounting pressure over recent months, Infantino intends to stand for a fourth consecutive term next March at the FIFA Congress. But there is uncertainty around his future after three confederations rejected Infantino's plan, which was then abandoned.

Among them was UEFA, which said it has lost confidence in Infantino and threatened to boycott future World Cups.

Vega, meanwhile, played for Tottenham between 1997 and 2001 and is the first person to publicly challenge the 56-year-old.

#834. LASK 3-6 Liverpool: Bradley Barcola breaks his duck in stunning style - but Reds must back up impressive performance in the league to regain confidence lost by Man City thumping, writes LEWIS STEELE

Published: 19:45 BST, 14 October 2026 | Updated: 20:58 BST, 14 October 2026

A mid-autumn trip to the sleepy Danubian city of Linz might not be the first outing to pop into mind when Liverpool fans look back on this era in several years – but it might just be an important checkpoint.

It was here in Austria’s third-largest city that the much-criticised £123million new boy Bradley Barcola got his Reds career off the mark with a slick hat-trick. And maybe for manager Andoni Iraola, it was the night the new manager’s style had its lift-off moment and all clicked together.

Another under-fire figure, Florian Wirtz, ran the show as the Reds put in a blistering, relentless display that choked the Austrian champions into submission. The scoreline was not reflective of Liverpool’s dominance on and off the ball.

They attacked at a breakneck speed and in merciless fashion, scoring three times in 16 first-half minutes, as Ronald Araujo’s 22nd-minute header started a rout that left poor LASK goalkeeper Lukas Jungwirth looking like he wanted to tap out and go home.

The victory helped blow away the cobwebs of any potential post-Manchester City hangover and, above all, injected some much-needed confidence into the legs of Liverpool’s attackers ahead of three testing league assignments against Brentford, Brighton and champions Arsenal.

‘I'm really happy for Bradley, because you were asking me yesterday about him, not getting the numbers, also Florian, and both of them today played really, really well,’ said Iraola.

Bradley Barcola opened his Liverpool account with a hat-trick against LASK on Wednesday

Lewis Koumas scored his first goal of the season on a confidence-boosting evening for Reds

But Liverpool will look to back up a fine showing against European minnows in the league next

‘They made a difference. Bradley, apart from the hat-trick I thought he was a threat, always when one-on-one, certainly in behind and he helped us a lot to control the game, finding the pockets. I am happy for both of them.

‘For their confidence for sure, it's very good. I think they feel now that we trust them a lot.

‘Bradley has to enjoy this. To score a hat-trick in the Champions League is always very difficult.

‘Even just in training, you could feel he was very lively, and sometimes you feel these things (are going to happen).’

Of course, this impressive performance will mean zero if it is not backed up in west London on Saturday. There have been glimpses of class in most games this season but the problem for new boss Iraola has been sustaining that high level or taking it into the next game.

Some will also point to the fact that this was LASK’s first-ever main-draw home game in the Champions League and argue Liverpool should be able to beat these rookies with ease. That might be true but let it take nothing away from the easy-on-the-eye performance.

After all, poor old Celtic rocked up here in the qualifying rounds and lost 5-1, a result that might be one to use in your next pub debate about where the Scottish champions would fare in English football.

Speaking of Glasgow, Barcola’s treble was the first away hat-trick for Liverpool since Mohamed Salah did so at Ibrox against Rangers four years ago. Barcola was unplayable and the away end sang about how he ‘runs down the wing for me’ to the tune of Buddy Holly’s Heartbeat.

In truth, he does a lot more than just making runs down the wing. He cuts inside, he can score goals, he is not selfish and enjoys link-up play, he is hard-working off the ball. Or, to summarise, he is a complete player who is a two-time European champion worth £123m for a reason.

Iraola was able to allow Barcola and fellow big-money attacker Wirtz to garner some belief in their ability after a week of being hounded from all quarters, while also giving a rest to some tired stars and handing out minutes to others.

Virgil van Dijk had to settle into the unfamiliar surroundings of the substitutes’ bench, the first league or Champions League game – that was not a meaningless dead-rubber – he had not started since September 2023, though he did come on to captain the Reds for a 200th time.

Jeremie Frimpong, severely lacking in confidence, scored one and assisted another two, while fellow full back Kostas Tsimikas, wearing the armband for an hour, managed two assists and proved his worth as a fine set-piece taker. Iraola will trust both more after this match.

And then there was the energetic, likeable local lad Lewis Koumas. The Wales international scored for the first time this season and, boy, did he deserve it after working his socks off and seeing two strikes chalked off for offside earlier on.

He had also made the assist for the first Barcola goal after canny work from 18-year-old Rio Ngumoha – one of two teenagers starting alongside Trey Nyoni. Barcola’s second showed his ingenuity to wriggle free from a defender, the third demonstrated his positional instinct.

LASK had a late rally with three late goals after Iraola had changed both centre backs, as substitute Florian Flecker scored two in three minutes.

Evidently, there are still a few minor teething problems for the new boss to iron out but this breathtaking attacking display will help.

#835. Man City appeal verdict 'expected early next year' - as Andy Burnham faces questions over 'freebies from Abu Dhabi deleted from public record'

Published: 14:03 BST, 14 October 2026 | Updated: 19:35 BST, 14 October 2026

Manchester City's appeal into their Premier League guilty verdict is expected to be heard by mid-January, according to the head of the Independent Football Regulator (IFR).

City were found guilty of all their alleged serious breaches of the Premier League's financial rules between 2009 and 2018 by an independent commission.

They were found to have made 'sham' agreements to manipulate their financial accounts to the tune of £900million over a nine-season period which saw them win eight trophies in the biggest cheating scandal in British sporting history.

The IFR could force owner Sheikh Mansour to sell the club, or bar any personnel from being owners or directors, once the appeal process is complete.

IFR chief David Kogan told Times Radio: 'The Premier League have said that they want to get this resolved within the season and actually, of course, it's not the Premier League, it's an independent commission that's going to hear this, made of three retired either judges or lawyers.

'My understanding is there is a prescribed process, which is 12 weeks, and so people are assuming this will actually be heard by the middle or the end of January. But as I say, it's not our process, it's that of the Premier League's independent commission. What I don't think we can do is take any judgment until we're quite clear.

Manchester City's appeal into their Premier League guilty verdict is expected to be heard by mid-January

Andy Burnham, then Greater Manchester mayor, pictured with Manchester City chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak in 2019

'Obviously, City claim that they have some form of silver bullet to put off these charges and win the appeal, and we're not there to judge whether that's right or wrong yet, but I think we'll know in the early part of next year.'

Kogan threatened to resign from his role if there is any political interference in the IFR dealing with the saga.

The IFR was created in September 2025 and was given the task of protecting and promoting the sustainability of English football.

But Andy Burnham has had to defend himself after being accused of 'covering up' links to Manchester City following a register of interests being 'deleted'.

Kogan added: 'The prime minister is capable of saying whatever he wants to say. You asked me whether we have had any interference politically in any of the judgments we're making, and I'm telling you, categorically, we have not.

'We will take a judgment based on evidence, once the appeal has been heard by the independent commission of the Premier League, we're going to look at that evidence closely, we're going to actually have powers of investigation ourselves, and that will be what governs what we do.'

City could face expulsion from the Premier League, a fine, a points deduction, and even having their trophies stripped.

But Prime Minister Burnham came out in support of the crisis-stricken club's Abu Dhabi owners... before backtracking and vowing to release all material from his dealings with them.

Independent Football Regulator chief David Kogan says he will resign if there is any political interference

Mr Burnham previously claimed to have had just one formal meeting with City chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak.

But he now stands accused of misleading the public after a deleted register of interest showed he joined Al Mubarak twice in a luxury box at City's Etihad Stadium, while he also accepted tickets to an Ed Sheeran concert, according to the BBC .

Mr Burnham accepted City-funded freebies worth nearly £1,200 which appeared on a register of interests that he signed in December 2020 during his time as Manchester mayor and was later taken down from the Greater Manchester Combined Authority (GMCA)'s website, they report.

On April 18, 2020, the register shows a value of £699 given to 'dinner with the Chairman at Man City/ Man United derby at the Etihad.'

And later that year on August 17, the entry reads: 'Dinner with Richard Leese and Chair of Man City for the Everton match at the Etihad.' The match ticket value is given as £38, while the hospitality is listed at £300.

At PMQs on Wednesday afternoon, Mr Burnham was asked: 'Did anyone associated with the running of Manchester City raise the charges they were facing and have now been found guilty of, either with him or any member of his team?'

The Prime Minister replied: 'They did not raise those issues with me. I'm very happy for everything to be set out in full, it is why I asked the Greater Manchester Combined Authority, in response to a call from the leader of the opposition and others to set out a full statement of my key dealings with the owners of Manchester City Football Club.

'That statement was published on Monday and it includes the issues in the news today and that is the position.'

GMCA has not yet responded to Daily Mail Sport's request for comment. According to the BBC, it is the GMCA's policy to only publish entries from the current mayoral term.

The details of Mr Burnham's contacts with City during his time as mayor were released by GMCA on Monday.

They revealed the Prime Minister had a formal meeting with Al Mubarak at an investment summit in October 2021 while he was Greater Manchester mayor. He also chatted to Al Mubarak in the stands during a testimonial game in 2019 and was accompanied by City staff on official overseas visits to China and Japan.

But the deleted register of interests shows he was in a hospitality suite at the Etihad with Al Mubarak for a game against Everton and also the Manchester derby.

Burnham had previously said on The Rest is Politics podcast: 'I will quite clearly put out there everything that I have done working with them in my previous role as Mayor of Greater Manchester.

'None of it is recent, in terms of meetings I had. I only had one significant meeting and that was in 2021. That is right and I will put that all out there.'

The new revelation will only intensify scrutiny over the Prime Minister's relationship with City's Abu Dhabi owners, who maintain their innocence and are appealing the independent commission's verdict.

The Guardian also reported on Wednesday that a club representative from City was invited on a government-backed trade delegation to India this week.

Bev Craig, who replaced Burnham as Manchester mayor, took a representative from the club to Delhi and Mumbai on a trip organised by business secretary Jonathan Reynolds.

Mrs Craig defended the decision, telling the newspaper it had played a key role in helping build infrastructure in her city.

'If a football club has broken the rules, a football club should be punished for breaking the rules, and that is pretty clear in an independent process,' she said.

'I think what can also be true at the same time though, if you ask residents in east Manchester, have they benefited from a new library, a new leisure centre, a new sixth-form college, infrastructure investment, the job opportunities that come from them being a good employment charter signee and an early adopter of the real living wage – then they will have felt that benefit.'

#836. BBC football pundit Shay Given marries his fiancée after 12-year engagement in stunning ceremony at Westminster Abbey - with special permission to use the royal church

By LUKE AUGUSTUS, ASSISTANT SPORTS EDITOR

Published: 12:35 BST, 12 October 2026 | Updated: 18:14 BST, 14 October 2026

Shay Given is a long-time Premier League star and now a staple of the BBC's football punditry team - but it was his new wife's connections which helped them tie the knot in their Westminster Abbey wedding this weekend.

The former Newcastle United and Republic of Ireland goalkeeper, 50, wed Rebecca Gibson on Saturday following a 12-year engagement.

The newlyweds were a picture of happiness on their momentous day as they said their vows at a venue that is a rarity for weddings.

Traditionally Westminster Abbey marriages can only take place there if the bride or groom have a recognised connection to the Abbey or who qualify under its established rules.

As a result, this applies to members of the Royal Family, members of the Order of the Bath and their children as well as residents of the Abbey precincts. If none of those three boxes are ticked, then the fourth and final route is others who meet specific qualifying criteria, subject to the Abbey's discretion.

In the case of Saturday's event, the wedding took place due to Gibson's connection  grandfather via her grandfather who is a former member of the Abbey community.

Shay Given married long-time fiancee Rebecca Gibson at Westminster Abbey on Saturday

The pair, who have two children together, had been engaged for 12 years before tying the knot

The newlyweds looked a picture of happiness as they tied the knot at the sacred venue

Gibson's grandfather Donald Buttress OBE was given a Lieutenant of the Victorian Order (LVO) in the 1997 New Year Honours before being awarded an OBE nine years later for services to the Conservation of Cathedrals.

For 11 years between 1988-1999 he was Surveyor of the Fabric of Westminster Abbey and in the forthcoming years also designed the Queen Mother Memorial on The Mall, which was unveiled in 2009.

In addition, Buttress - who turned 94 in April - lived at Westminster Abbey between 1998 and 1999 with Gibson often visiting her grandparents there as a young girl and exploring many hidden parts of the building, as she noted on Instagram once.

Their two daughters Gracie and Cassie were bridesmaids, as well as Sienna from Given's first marriage to Jane Cunningham. Given and Cunningham also have a son together called Shayne. Given wore a tuxedo, while Gibson wore an elegant dress made by New York designer Tom Sebastien. The wedding itself was curated by The Bridal PA, owned by Amy Ramsey.

After the wedding, Gibson and Given - who met while she was working in PR - held an after party at Hotel Cafe Royal.

Gibson's grandfather Donald Buttress OBE has a strong connection with the Royal Family

Given enjoyed a brilliant Premier League career, which included a fine spell as Newcastle's No 1

Given is widely regarded as one of the greatest Irish goalkeepers of all-time and enjoyed a stellar playing career for the likes of Newcastle United, Manchester City, Aston Villa, Stoke City and Blackburn Rovers in the Premier League - amassing 451 appearances in the English top flight.

Since retiring, Given has turned his hand to TV punditry with his work including BBC Sport.

#838. Wayne Rooney's transfer request regret, Roy Keane's bust-up with Fergie and the interview that spelt the end for Cristiano Ronaldo - the warning signs for Lisandro Martinez after his Madrid meltdown

Published: 15:49 BST, 14 October 2026 | Updated: 17:32 BST, 14 October 2026

As if things weren't bad enough for Michael Carrick after Man United were beaten by Atletico Madrid in the Champions League on Tuesday night, Lisandro Martinez plunged his beleaguered manager into further trouble with an astonishing post-match rant.

In it, the Argentine defender hit out at United's performance in Spain, insisted Carrick was 'doing his best', and accused the club's hierarchy of not backing the team enough.

'I expect more (investment) 100 per cent,' Martinez said. 'I expect more from our technical director. I have to control myself a lot but sometimes is a reflection of the mirror of how is our club at the moment.

'We did a fantastic season last season and now we expect more from the top; more players to compete because many teams bring many players as well. We created the base to create an amazing team. It is annoying and disappointing coming here and I am not seeing my team trying to get an amazing result.'

It remains to be seen if there are any ramifications for Martinez, but it all adds to the sense of crisis surrounding Old Trafford right now.

So, in light of Martinez's comments, Daily Mail Sport has taken a look at previous examples of United stars calling out the club – and what happened to them.

Lisandro Martinez called out Man United's hierarchy after their defeat by Atletico Madrid

The defeat in Spain heaped the pressure on under-fire Red Devils boss Michael Carrick

Jaap Stam was a key part of United's famous Treble-winning team in 1998-99, making his abrupt departure to Lazio in 2001 all the more shocking.

That came after the Dutch defender released an autobiography in August of that year, with some of the claims in it reportedly upsetting Sir Alex Ferguson.

Stam made statements about his views on opposition players and team-mates, while he alleged that Ferguson's approach to buy him in 1998 had been done without the permission of his former team PSV.

Ferguson was incensed and dropped Stam from his squad shortly before his departure, which at the time was put down to a generous offer from Lazio and a dip in form after an Achilles issue.

Years later, Ferguson admitted it was a mistake but his views at the time were no doubt affected by the release of Stam's autobiography.

Jaap Stam (right) left United shortly after the release of his controversial autobiography

Roy Keane's exit from United 21 years ago was hugely explosive and came after a period where tensions between him and Sir Alex Ferguson had been rising.

Things came to a head following a 4-1 defeat by Middlesbrough at the start of November 2005, after which Keane appeared on MUTV and savagely ripped into his team-mates.

This included his brutal description of Rio Ferdinand, then United's record signing, when he said: 'Just because you are paid £120,000-a-week and play well for 20 minutes against Tottenham, you think you are a superstar.'

His comments were so inflammatory that Ferguson and United CEO David Gill ensured the interview was never broadcast. Those present had described the interview as 'explosive even by Keane's standards'.

His departure was confirmed by mutual consent a few weeks later, yet despite the dramatic ending, Keane was given a testimonial by United and Ferguson spoke highly of him after his retirement was confirmed in June 2006.

Roy Keane left United shortly after an inflammatory interview about his team-mates on MUTV

Wayne Rooney may be United's record goalscorer after 13 years of glorious service, yet things could have been so different following the saga around his future in 2010.

Frustrated by the high-profile sales of Cristiano Ronaldo and Carlos Tevez the previous summer, Rooney raised doubts over the club's ambition in a statement after Ferguson revealed the forward wanted to leave.

Rooney claimed that in meetings, Gill and the Red Devils boss 'did not give me any assurances' over the future of the squad and the 'continued ability of the club to attract the top players in the world', insisting this wasn't about money.

Amid links to Man City, some fans protested outside Rooney's Cheshire mansion, with one banner reading: 'If you join City you're dead'.

But, in a dramatic u-turn days later following intense talks, Rooney signed a new five-year contract after receiving the assurances he craved.

Rooney later admitted his actions were wrong, and he went on to spend seven more years at Old Trafford before joining Everton in 2017.

United legend Wayne Rooney almost left in 2010 after handing in a transfer request

Cristiano Ronaldo's triumphant return to United in the summer of 2021 quickly turned sour, with the legendary Portuguese star leaving the club just over a year later after his contract was terminated.

Having grown frustrated with what he witnessed on and off the pitch, Ronaldo fell out with Erik ten Hag early on in the 2022-23 season.

So furious was Ronaldo that he gave an unsanctioned interview to Piers Morgan in November 2022.

Across the two-part chat, Ronaldo claimed he had 'no respect' for Ten Hag, insisted he felt 'betrayed' by the club and said that the Glazers 'do not care' about United.

He also hit out at his critics, which included former team-mates Gary Neville and Wayne Rooney, and made several other damning allegations.

Within a week of the interview airing, Ronaldo left the club by 'mutual agreement' without a pay-off, and he went on to join Al-Nassr in Saudi Arabia.

Cristiano Ronaldo left United in November 2022 after falling out with boss Erik ten Hag

When Jadon Sancho joined United from Borussia Dortmund in 2021 for £73million, it was one of the most anticipated Premier League transfers in years.

But things never got going for Sancho, and despite him eventually leaving on a free transfer this summer, his last Premier League appearance for United came on August 26, 2023, with a key moment coming a week later when they faced Arsenal.

Sancho was left out of the matchday squad that day, and ten Hag said post-match this was due to poor performances in training.

The winger immediately hit back on social media, saying the claims were 'completely untrue' and insisted he was being made a 'scapegoat' by the club.

Jadon Sancho famously spoke out against Erik ten Hag but things didn't work out well for him

Sancho appeared to choose the wrong man to take on, as, after refusing to apologise, he was banished from the first-team by ten Hag.

Sancho went on to join Dortmund on loan the following January, before successive season-long stints at Chelsea and Aston Villa.

He did feature once more for United – in the 2024 Community Shield – but the fact he was also deemed surplus to requirements under ten Hag's successor Ruben Amorim suggested that speaking out didn't work well.

Published: 17:00 BST, 14 October 2026 | Updated: 17:00 BST, 14 October 2026

Talks have accelerated between Jacob Murphy and Newcastle and the winger is ready to sign improved terms to the summer of 2028

Joe Willock could be sold in the new year if his contract situation remains as is

Newcastle winger Athony Elanga is making good progress with his rehab after injury and is set to rejoin training shortly

Nick Woltemade will NOT be returning to Newcastle in January, despite speculation in Italy that Juventus could look to cut short his loan deal.

Woltemade is yet to start in Serie A and his only goal came from the penalty spot in the Europa League. His performances have triggered some debate in Turin and former Juve midfielder Alessio Tacchinardi has this week suggested the club need to sign a recognised striker.

Woltemade’s £3.5m loan move and coverage of his wages helped Newcastle fund the £51m signing of Matias Fernandez-Pardo from a Squad Cost Ratio perspective for this season, and there is little chance of the German returning to Tyneside during this campaign.

Fernandez-Pardo started the final 11 matches of last season at centre forward and that is where he sees his future, starting the last three in the position for Newcastle. He had previously played predominantly out wide, mainly on the left.

Newcastle's £51m signing Matias Fernandez-Pardo wants to play as a centre forward despite the debate surrounding his best position

North Shields band Hector Gannet provide the vocals, while the organ of St Nicholas Cathedral and Northumbrian piper Chris Ormston feature in a track designed to return the song to its folk roots.

The tempo on the pitch will be of greater concern come kick-off, however.
