Arsenal have told staff they are planning to cut 60 jobs, just months after the club ended their 22-year wait for the Premier League title.

The redundancies will focus on off-field areas, and not affect the coaching or backroom staff of the men's or women's teams, the club’s community operation, the Arsenal Foundation and security staff.

The news comes just a week after Arsenal announced Mikel Arteta had signed a lucrative four-year contract worth around £20million per year, making him the highest paid manager in the top flight.

Staff were told by the club on Tuesday that 60 jobs will be cut

The north London club’s recent financial margins have also been healthy, bringing the controversial decision into question.

For the 2021-22 post-Covid season, Arsenal posted a revenue of £367million which increased to a record £691m in the 2024-25 campaign.

This figure will have likely reached the £800m mark in the 2025-26 season which saw the Gunners win the league and reach the Champions League final.

Losing to Paris Saint-Germain in the Budapest final alone netted the Gunners £16m, though the club also paid out millions in bonuses to players as part of their contracts.

While winning the title helped them to a total of almost £200m in prize-money last year, they will also have paid out millions in bonuses to players as part of their contracts.

High-profile departures in recent months include chief commercial officer Juliet Slot and long-serving general counsel Svenja Geissmar.

The exit of Slot was a particular surprise given her contribution to Arsenal’s commercial boom. During her tenure, commercial revenue rose sharply, rising from £142m in 2021-22 to £263.2m in 2024-25, as the club sought to capitalise on its return to the Champions League and resurgence under Arteta.

Slot oversaw a series of lucrative partnership renewals, including with Adidas and Emirates.

#843. Football fan, 62, is found NOT guilty of deliberately throwing himself off a stadium's upper tier in bizarre FA Cup incident which left a woman injured - after drinking five cans of lager before the lunchtime game

Published: 14:02 BST, 14 October 2026 | Updated: 14:02 BST, 14 October 2026

A football fan who admitted to drinking five cans of lager before falling from the upper tier of a stand onto rival supporters below has been found not guilty of assault.

John Ryan, 62, broke down in tears at Ipswich Crown Court after the jury returned verdicts of not guilty, saying the court case had been 'very stressful'.

Maidstone United fan Ryan had attended Ipswich's Portman Road to back the non-league side in their FA Cup clash against the Tractor Boys in January 2024.

During the celebrations of a Maidstone goal, Ryan ended up on the edge of the upper tier roof, before falling onto Ipswich fans below. Joanne Peters and her partner Aaron Rose were left injured.

Ryan had been one of thousands of travelling fans backing the FA Cup underdogs in Suffolk, which he described in court as 'the biggest match in the club's history'.

The jury heard how he had been in the Cobbold Stand upper tier when the 'special' goal went in, before he fell, slid down the sloping roof above the hospitality boxes and landed on Ipswich fans below.

A football fan, 62, has been accused of deliberately launching himself at rival fans from a roof

Limbs from the Maidstone fans today 😂 #itfc #mufc #FACup pic.twitter.com/MKr8aVz5YV

The 62-year-old - who told the court he drank five cans of lager before the 12.30pm fixture - told the jury he had been unsure whether he had been pushed or his foot had slipped when he fell.

Ryan was found not guilty of one count of assault by beating and one count of actual bodily harm.

Following the verdict, he told reporters:'When you score a goal like that the last thing on your mind is what's going to happen.

'I just remember going down the stairs and I hit that barrier, fell over it and that was it.'

Asked if he would like to say anything to Peters and Rose, Ryan said: 'I'm sorry, it was an accident.

'I'm sorry it happened, what more can I say?'
